513519|2026-09.headline: Pitti Engineering Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.3% to INR581 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.8% on forex, fuel/power and raw material costs.
513519|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR581 crore (up 16.3% YoY) and H1 revenue about INR1,110 crore (up roughly 15%), with results now reported standalone after merging two subsidiaries in September 2026. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to INR91 crore, but margin was 15.8%, hit by a INR4.61 crore forex loss, higher consumables/packing, fuel and power costs, and higher employee costs ahead of new capacity. Adjusted PAT fell to INR36 crore from INR43 crore, as Q2 FY26 included INR21 crore of Maharashtra incentive income that is now deferred to next year. Management announced a new INR450 crore lamination and machining capex (to FY31) on top of the INR290 crore Hyderabad project, and reiterated FY27 guidance.

Maharashtra incentive: management expects about INR40 crore per year recovery from next year, pursuing a 9-year period instead of the 7-year sanction.
capex_capacity: New INR450 crore capex (INR125 crore land and building for Bangalore consolidation, INR325 crore for capacity) to take sheet metal capacity to 160,000 tpa (from 108,000) and machining to 1.31 million hours by FY31, phased to FY31.
Earlier INR290 crore Hyderabad greenfield casting and machining project, phased through FY30; cumulative INR740 crore, of which about INR250-260 crore is committed (land and buildings), rest modular.

demand_pricing: Management says demand remained robust despite Middle East-related inflation and supply chain disruption.

Railways supported by North American rail modernisation; mining and off-highway demand supporting machine components.
Raw material (steel) prices rising; steel is passed through quarterly, while fuel and power pass-through is annual.

Top five to seven customers (grouped by beneficial ownership) remain the bulk of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much was the forex loss, and what was the prior quarter's figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 forex loss was INR4.61 crore, booked in other expenses above EBITDA. Q1 FY27 figure not available on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover to 16-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel and power costs to be passed on from January and expected to normalise by Q4; steel is a quarterly pass-through. Inflation depresses percentage margin even when passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the trade payables increase sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Trade payables rose to INR470 crore from INR236 crore; management intends to lean on payables rather than cash for materials ahead of the capex cycle.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR450 crore capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately INR150 crore in FY28, rest linked to demand through FY31; management believes it can be funded from internal accruals, with debt as the flexible option.

qa_highlights.question: Why defer the Maharashtra incentive?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanction is for 7 years (INR57 crore per year), while local sales support about INR35-36 crore per year; management is seeking a 9-year period (INR44 crore per year) and expects about INR40 crore per year next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin at FY31 capacity?

514043|2026-03.headline: Himatsingka Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose about 5.8% to INR721 crores, with management pivoting into yarn, fabric and apparel adjacencies.
514043|2026-03.overview: Consolidated total income was INR721 crores against INR681 crores a year earlier, up about 5.8%. Q4 other income of about INR100 crores was mostly foreign exchange gains of roughly INR95 crores from rupee depreciation. Utilisation was 99% in spinning, 56% in sheeting and 63% in Terry Towel, with delayed outbound shipments to some jurisdictions and Middle East impacts expected to persist into Q1 FY27. Management framed FY26 as volatile due to US tariffs and the Middle East war, and announced a shift toward yarn, fabric and apparel solutions using existing infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: What capacity and business plans sit behind the new yarn, fabric and apparel verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will leverage existing infrastructure (spinning, fabric debottlenecking, meeting capacity, shipping and knitting) and serve third-party clients; apparel is an adjacency via existing cut-and-sew infrastructure, to be explored conservatively.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new verticals absorb capacity currently used for home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn solutions will be better served to third parties than used in home textiles, citing expected market and pricing pressure in home textiles.

qa_highlights.question: What are the near-term and medium-term margin trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-term EBITDA margin band of 18-22% reiterated; near-term inflation from the war may dampen margins by a small percentage, and it treats other income as part of the picture, noting a mix of realised and unrealised gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction target and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Next target is net debt of about INR2,000 crores from about INR2,550 crores, within the next 12 months, via ordinary cash flows and capital market initiatives.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue and margin can the new verticals deliver, and what capex is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Infrastructure can deliver about INR4,000 crores of top line and INR700-800 crores of EBITDA at optimal utilisation, reached in 18-24 months; home textiles to be about half the portfolio; margins comparable; no major capex.

514043|2026-06.headline: Himatsingka Q1 FY27 consolidated total income fell to INR634 crores from INR661 crores, with EBITDA of INR101 crores (~16% margin).
514043|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income was INR634 crores against INR661 crores, described as range-bound, with shipment deferrals linked to Middle East geopolitical issues and lower capacity utilisation in some divisions. EBITDA came in at INR101 crores, a margin of about 16%, attributed to lower revenue, product mix tweaks and raw material inflation. Management said the call was mainly about the strategic transition to a multi-vertical model using existing assets: Yarn Solutions and Fabric Solutions have started and are ramping up, Apparel Solutions is due a couple of quarters out, and Home Textiles (especially Sheeting) will be rightsized. Net leverage was described as range-bound at about INR2,550 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What are the positives and negatives this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Negatives were revenue and offtake overhangs; positive is the start of the transition to the new multi-vertical model, which needs no expansion or capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise so much debt and how do tariffs affect the US business?
qa_highlights.answer: The recent NCD raise balances debt tenors and maturities and is not incremental capital. US tariff policy flip-flops created inflation and altered demand; tariff outlook has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: How will fabric capacity of 90 million meters be used versus the 61 million meters home capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The 61 million meters excluded knit platforms; combined 90 million meters will be allocated between Home Textile Sheeting and Fabric Solutions from common infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: How much yarn capacity will be sold externally and is more capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 90% of yarn capacity to be sold externally; capex kept to maintenance and organic needs only.

qa_highlights.question: Will lost Home Textile revenue be replaced in the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for range-bound revenue, but Sheeting will be rightsized; Yarn and Fabric each target about INR1,000 crores at full capacity (about INR2,000 crores combined), with no quarterly split disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Sheeting ramp-down about profitability or US challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: US market share loss, tariff-driven pricing pressure and client concentration led to repositioning the business as Himatsingka 2.0.

514183|2026-03.headline: Black Rose Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% and EBITDA about 90% YoY, with EBITDA margin up to 11% from 9.7%, helped by stock-and-sale model and price normalisation.
514183|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 showed a sharp jump, with revenue up 38% and EBITDA up about 90%, driven by the stock-and-sale model in distribution and growth in manufacturing. For the full year, standalone revenue dipped slightly as chemical prices corrected from the start of the year through March 2026, while volumes grew in domestic distribution and acrylamide liquid and NMA. The company stayed debt-free, inventories fell, and a 125% dividend was recommended. Management declined to give FY27 EBITDA or revenue numbers, saying only that top line is targeted to grow over FY26 at current prices.

514211|2026-06.headline: Sumeet Industries Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 3.24% (EBITDA INR8.85 crore) on raw material volatility, while management guides ~6% margin and 30%+ revenue growth for FY27.
514211|2026-06.overview: Revenue (income) rose over 9% YoY to INR272.74 crore, but EBITDA was INR8.85 crore (3.24% margin) and PAT was INR1.14 crore, which management attributed to crude-driven PTA/MEG volatility, higher freight costs and a 15-day maintenance shutdown. Production fell 17% QoQ, with sales supported by inventory liquidation. Management said the rights issue (INR199.75 crore gross, net ~INR194.90 crore) is being deployed to working capital, the Nakoda CP plant, debt repayment (~INR23 crore) and a 6.5 MW solar plant. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 30%+ revenue growth, ~6% EBITDA margin and 3.5–4% PAT margin, with the Nakoda plant now guided for Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited long-term debt of INR86 crore and short-term borrowings of INR74 crore (pre-repayment). After ~INR23 crore repayment, remaining machine term loan expected around INR30 crore; finance cost expected to fall significantly, with CC interest near negligible.

514234|2026-03.headline: Sangam India FY26 revenue crossed INR3,200 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR83 crore; Q4 PAT INR33 crore on INR880 crore revenue.
514234|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a rebuild year, with revenue, EBITDA and PAT rising sequentially from Q1 through Q4. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR880 crore, EBITDA INR98 crore and PAT INR33 crore. Management attributed profit growth to high capacity utilisation and operational efficiency, and denied any one-time inventory gain in Q4 despite the West Asia war lifting crude-linked input prices. Management is preparing a new capex cycle but has not finalised it; renewable power and captive fibre are the stated priorities.

Yarn capacity utilisation is about 95%. PV yarn is mostly domestic, with 10-15% exports; March shipments to some regions were delayed and freight costs rose.

segments.name: Garments
segments.commentary: Garment utilisation is about 50%, the highest in six to eight quarters, with management expecting further gains. C9 brand accounts for 40-45% of garment business and contract manufacturing for the balance.

segments.name: Recycled polyester fibre
segments.commentary: In-house recycled fibre meets about 50% of polyester fibre needs, processing close to 40,000 metric tons of plastic waste a year. Green fibre is reported at about 97% utilisation. Management targets 75-80% in-house share.

segments.commentary: About 50% of denim raw material is sourced in-house; management plans more capacity here.

Management said yarn exports are being reduced by strategy and shifting to fabric exports.

qa_highlights.answer: Top-line growth similar to FY26 (run-rate of Q4 times four plus inflation); no abnormal growth expected given high utilisation.

qa_highlights.answer: Renewable share about 10-15% now, targeted at 70%+ by around June 2027; cumulative EBITDA benefit INR50-60 crore annually once commissioned.

514448|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% YoY to a record quarter on ~16% volume growth; EBITDA margin held near 27% before VAM-driven price hikes.
514448|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 18% YoY on nearly 16% volume growth, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with EBITDA margin steady at about 27%. FY26 volume growth was about 8% against 11% in FY25. Raw material VAM prices roughly doubled (management cited INR 80-75 earlier versus INR 160-180 now), and the company has passed through about 60-70% of the increase via price hikes effective early April and 1 May, with a further hike from around 15 May. Management declined to give explicit FY27 guidance, but said it aims for 15-20% volume growth to reach INR 500 crore revenue in two to three years. Receivable days rose to about 150-160 days, which management attributes to new-state dealer build-out and expects to normalise over two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: VAM is crude-linked and price roughly doubled; 60-70% of the increase is being passed through, with the 1 May hike effective from the start of May and a further hike around 15 May. Normalisation could take about three months if the situation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Advertising spend plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Advertising and trade marketing was ~4% of revenue (INR 50-54 crore); target is 6-7% for at least three years, with 70-80% in trade marketing and 20-25% in brand communication.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: New states need two to three years of dealer engagement; receivable days were ~150-160 against ~120 in FY24-25; management expects control within two to three quarters, with ~1% bad debts historically.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold a large FD / liquid balance rather than pay higher dividends or buy back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has paid 15% of PAT as dividend for six years and retains cash for expansion and market share gains; liabilities of INR 90-95 crore are also tied to the carpenter loyalty programme.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand weakening from price hikes, and how does the furniture-cost share affect demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said uptake is normal with some carpenter migration for about one to two months; adhesives are 5-10% of furniture cost, and redemptions remain high.

514448|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY (about 10% volume, 7% price) while EBITDA margin fell to about 14.4% on raw material spike.
514448|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 17% YoY in Q1 FY27, with roughly 10% from volumes and about 7% from price increases taken in April and mid-May. EBITDA margin compressed to about 14.4%, which management attributed to 6-7 percentage points of raw material cost inflation (VAM spike linked to West Asia tensions) plus about 3-4 points of aggressive dealer-meet and sales promotion spend. Management guided back to a 22-25% EBITDA range longer term and said it is too early to commit to 28-29% in Q2. Working capital weakened, with receivables around INR 145-150 crore (debtor days above 150) and inventory higher, and management targets 120 days over the next two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sales promotion and employee costs rise sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales force raised from 520 to 562, new hires and April appraisals; about INR 4.5 crore spent on 54 dealer meets in 45 days (vs about INR 2 crore for 30 meets last year).

qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say; management is targeting the 22-25% range longer term and said raw material cooling has begun but not returned to earlier levels.

qa_highlights.question: What share of growth came from volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% from volume and about 7% from price in Q1; management expects price contribution may not persist if realisations normalise, and aims for 15-20% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth weak in FY24-FY26 after the COVID-era surge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a consolidation phase after an 80% jump to INR 181 crore; it cited FY25 and FY26 growth of about 9-10% and two quarters above 15% in the last four.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and debtor days outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables about INR 145-150 crore; target 120 days in two to three quarters, with slower push to protect retailer relationships in newer states; cited bad debt below 0.5%.

516003|2026-03.headline: Duroply Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5% YoY to ₹111.6 cr, but PBT fell to ₹1.03 cr after a ₹27.5 lakh wage-code exceptional loss and EBITDA slipped to ₹5.18 cr.
516003|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹111.6 cr, up 5% YoY and 20% QoQ, with in-house manufactured goods at ₹61.9 cr (+4% YoY) and contract manufacturing at ₹49.7 cr (+6.7% YoY, roughly +50% QoQ). Gross margin fell to 34.3% from 37% in Q3 FY26 and 34.9% a year earlier, and EBITDA was ₹5.18 cr versus ₹5.4 cr in both Q3 FY26 and Q4 FY25. For FY26, revenue grew 8.3% to ₹402.6 cr, EBITDA rose 25.3% to ₹22.4 cr, and working-capital days improved across debtors, inventory and payables. Management said H2 FY26 growth slowed and that corrective actions are under way, while flagging high input-cost inflation linked to the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of geopolitical tensions on the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Chemical input costs (melamine, urea, phenol) are elevated, the dollar has weakened, and freight, fuel and labour costs are rising, so high inflation is expected in the coming months; as a branded player, the company can pass on much of it but with limits.

qa_highlights.question: Have costs been passed on in April and May?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost increases from March and April were largely passed on, May partially; consumer resistance to further price increases is now emerging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sector outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Plywood grows about 6-7% a year and the organised segment 10-11%; management sees a strong long-term 8-10 year outlook despite near-term input-cost pressure from wood, imported timber and petrochemicals.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins be affected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes not; it is working to control COGS and believes it can procure better given sufficient liquidity, aims for EBITDA margin expansion, but said raw material impact is hard to predict.

qa_highlights.question: Any quantitative guidance for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 9-12% quantitative growth over the next two years, made up of 10-12% volume growth plus price, described as conservative.

516072|2026-06.headline: Vishnu Chemicals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24.9% YoY to INR433.4 crores, but EBITDA margin slipped to 15.1% from 16.1%.
516072|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating revenue grew 24.9% YoY to INR433.4 crores and PAT rose 23% to INR39.6 crores, while EBITDA margin fell to 15.1% from 16.1%. Management attributed the sequential moderation to a roughly three-week Vizag maintenance shutdown and a one-off barium baryte price adjustment of close to INR8 crores for the prior two years. Management expects freight costs to stay elevated in Q2 because of West Asia tensions and gave no quarterly or full-year margin guidance, while reiterating a 20% long-term EBITDA margin target. Chromium mix shift, strontium ramp-up and the South Africa chrome mine restart are the main levers cited for H2 FY27.

517041|2026-03.headline: Ador Welding Q4 FY26: revenue up ~3% YoY, EBITDA ~INR38 crore (+200 bps), with management guiding to 100–200 bps further EBITDA margin gains.
517041|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 revenue growth of about 3% YoY, EBITDA of about INR38 crore (up 200 bps) and gross margin of about 36%, excluding the Kuwait recovery and exceptional items. The Flares and Process Equipment division has been folded into a single welding segment, with loss-making large projects being wound down in favour of product-line business. Management declined to give formal guidance, but flagged Middle East dispatch disruption in March, a Saudi market that is now the third-largest export market, and a longer-term aspiration to triple earnings.

517059|2026-03.headline: Salzer Q4 FY26 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 474 crore, but margins fell to 7% on petrochemical and copper cost pressure; FY27 EBITDA guidance is 9-9.5%.
517059|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 474 crore, with EBITDA excluding other income of INR 31 crore (7% margin) and PAT of INR 10 crore. FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR 1,758 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 8% and PAT grew only 3% to INR 54 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to plastic (petrochemical-linked) cost increases of 2-3% of margin, copper and silver increases, freight and Middle East disruption. Working capital reached about 30% of revenue against a stated 25% ceiling, and management guided to a return to 25% in FY27.

segments.commentary: 56% of FY26 revenue and 51% of Q4; grew 20% YoY in FY26 and 15% in Q4. EBITDA margin 11% in FY26 and 8% in Q4; management says switchgear gross margin is about 35-40%.

segments.name: Wires and cables
segments.commentary: About 39% of FY26 revenue and 43% of Q4; grew 30% YoY in FY26 and 42% in Q4. EBITDA margin 5% in FY26 and 4% in Q4, with nearly all sales B2B.

segments.name: Building products
segments.commentary: About 5% of FY26 revenue and 6% of Q4; grew 16% YoY in FY26 and 36% in Q4.

segments.name: EV charging (Ultrafast Chargers, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 100 chargers sold, generating roughly INR 9 crore revenue to date; orders for close to 100 DC fast chargers held. Currently break-even at low volumes, targeted 12-15% EBITDA margin at scale; FY27 revenue expected around INR 25 crore.

segments.name: Smart metering
segments.commentary: About INR 45 crore of business executed over the last year; no large long-term orders secured yet. Addressable market about 17 crore meters, with AMISP requirements of 2-3 crore meters under discussion. No FY27 smart meter guidance given.

segments.commentary: INR 200 crore Bangalore Corporation street-lighting automation project under execution; revenue expected to start in Q2 FY27 at a steady monthly run rate.

Margins expected to be under pressure in Q1 FY27 and stabilise from Q2 FY27; switchgear EBITDA margin expected at 12-13% from Q2 onwards.
Existing-business revenue expected at INR 2,000-2,100 crore in FY27, excluding smart meter upside.
June 2026 price increase of 7-10% across products, after a roughly 15% increase in February 2026; management expects 100% cost pass-through over the two increases.
Exports targeted at about 25% of FY27 revenue; Middle East and Africa exports of about INR 24 crore expected to double over FY27-28.
Interest cost expected to rise at least 10% in FY27 on higher working capital; depreciation flat. Average short-term borrowing cost about 8%.
Working capital to return to 25% or below of revenue in FY27; target ROCE of about 18%, with management implying 18-20% by FY30.
capex_capacity: Saudi Arabia manufacturing plant delayed about six months by the Middle East conflict from February 2026; capital equipment ordered, expected by August 2026, with operations from September or October 2026.

In-house fully integrated EMS facility installed for PCB assembly for smart meters.
Aurawin SPV formed with a smart-metering market participant to act as a bidding company for future tenders.
Management said it is not yet giving a smart meter guidance and expects some orders, but is holding inventory currently.
demand_pricing: Management expects Indian electrical equipment market to grow at double digits over the next four to five years, driven by electrification, data centres, renewables, EV charging and smart meter rollout.

Price increase in February 2026 of about 15% did not fully offset costs; plastic price increase in Q4 to be offset only with the June 2026 price increase. Market accepted the February increase smoothly, per management.

Exports grew about 5% YoY in FY26; US tariffs cut exports about 6% and Middle East crisis reduced business by around 10-12%. Americas and Europe together make up about half of exports. UK benefits from favourable currency and zero import duty.

Competitive position: management says Salzer is in the top three in most products on quality and pricing, and commands a premium in some categories; competitors include foreign, Chinese and other country players.
Largest client concentration is Schneider Electric at about 12% of revenue (includes business formerly with L&T).

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance given recent price hikes and April volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance cut to 9-9.5% for FY27 (whole year). A further 7-10% price increase in June 2026 is planned; Q1 pressure expected, with margin stabilising in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the wires and cables EBITDA margin so low, and does the segment cover its interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly B2B (about 70% per the answer), and copper cost rise means a fixed absolute profit is now a lower percentage (margin was 6.5-7% a couple of years ago). Management said the business earns about 2-3% PAT after interest.

qa_highlights.question: Would management consider demerging wires and cables or other shareholder value unlocking steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the suggestion was taken positively and would be looked at, with no commitment or timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital and short-term debt risen, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital reached about 30% of revenue versus a 25% ceiling, due to margin erosion, smart meter capex and slow scale-up. Management expects a return to 25% or below in FY27. Receivable days are 90-95 on net sales basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi plant business model and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant aimed at local content requirements in Saudi projects; delayed about six months; Phase-1 capex about INR 15 crore; target INR 100 crore revenue for GCC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the EV charging business margins and revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently break-even due to low volumes; target EBITDA 12-15% at scale; FY27 revenue expected about INR 25 crore.

risks_watch: Petrochemical-linked plastic and copper/silver costs; Q1 FY27 margins expected to remain under pressure before the June price increase takes effect.
Working capital and short-term borrowing (INR 503 crore) versus the 25% of revenue target; interest cost expected to rise at least 10% in FY27.
Smart meter execution remains slow, with no large long-term orders secured and inventory being held.
Middle East conflict affecting Saudi plant timeline and exports; US tariffs reducing export volumes.
Saudi plant commissioning (August-October 2026) and the INR 200 crore Bangalore project revenue starting in Q2 FY27.
Shareholder value concerns over low wires and cables returns and the possible demerger, which management has not committed to.

517059|2026-06.headline: Salzer Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR498 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 6% and management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 8-8.5% from 10%.
517059|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR498 crore, led by industrial switchgear, wires and cables, and building products. EBITDA (excluding other income) fell to INR31 crore from INR42 crore, with margin at 6%, and PAT dropped to INR8 crore from INR17 crore (2% margin). Management attributed the compression to copper, silver and plastic input inflation with a lag in passing costs to customers in switchgear, which is not on a cost-plus model. Management now expects margins to normalise from Q3 with FY27 EBITDA around 8-8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA target of 10% in the investor presentation still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target would be toned down to about 8-8.5% for the full year, with Q3 and Q4 at 9-9.5%. An analyst objected to the mismatch with the presentation, and management agreed to correct it.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the price hikes has been accepted, and what is still pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases of April have been passed through, June increases take effect from August, and another increase is planned for September. Pending orders create a lag in pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Will annuity income from the energy project lift margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Annuity is about INR2 crore per month, with Salzer receiving around 50%. It is recorded as an associate, so management does not expect it to change the margin percentage significantly.

qa_highlights.question: Can cost-plus pricing or hedging protect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids cost-plus on standard switchgear to avoid opening cost sheets to customers, and does not hedge commodities beyond natural inventory hedging.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Wire & Cable margin stable while switchgear is not?
qa_highlights.answer: Wire & Cable is about 70% white-labelled on a cost-plus basis, so margins are stable. Switchgear is not cost-plus, and margin fell about 4.5 percentage points over two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Smart Meters and the Tamil Nadu tender?
qa_highlights.answer: Smart Meter revenue to date is about INR3.5 crore, with about INR22 crore of finished goods and pending orders awaiting customer clearance. The Tamil Nadu tender was cancelled, and management expects new tenders in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi plant revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Operations expected in September-October, with FY28 revenue of about INR25 crore, largely transferred from existing revenue.

517146|2026-03.headline: Usha Martin Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 52% to INR 212 crore at a 21.6% margin on revenue up 9.3% to INR 979 crore.
517146|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9.3% YoY to INR 979 crore, with operating EBITDA up 52% to INR 212 crore and margin at 21.6%, the highest since the steel business sale. FY26 revenue reached INR 3,691 crore (+6.2%) with operating EBITDA of INR 705 crore (19.1% margin vs 17.2%). Rope volume growth was only about 5% in Q4 because Middle East demand fell short by roughly 900 tons, and LRPC revenue fell 20.4%. The company ended FY26 with a net cash position of INR 332 crore, standalone operations debt-free, and guided to 10-12% volume growth and a 20% margin benchmark.

517146|2026-06.headline: Usha Martin Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore and EBITDA grew 44% to INR 208 crore at a 20.1% margin.
517146|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44% to INR 208 crore and margin up 380 bps YoY to 20.1%. Value grew faster than volume, driven by pass-through of input costs, a richer mix of value-added rope and plasticated LRPC, and a higher rope share. Wire rope volumes were marginally down as the Middle East fell about 28%, while India, the US and Europe grew. Operating cash flow was about INR 242 crore (116% of EBITDA), and free cash flow was INR 135 crore after INR 73 crore capex. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 10-12% rope volume growth and about 15% value growth, with a 20% minimum EBITDA margin base.

segments.name: Wire Rope
segments.commentary: Revenue up 18% YoY with value growth of 18% and marginally lower volumes; value-added rope share rose to 73% from 70% in FY26. Domestic rope volume up about 12% and value up about 21%. Middle East volume fell about 28% while realisations rose about 36%, holding revenue broadly flat.

segments.name: Wire and Strand (Wires)
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 19% and revenue up about 32% YoY; largely domestic, with early European supply in automotive and rockfall protection. Wire realisation about INR 85,000 per ton.

segments.name: LRPC (black and plasticated)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 3.9% YoY despite a volume decline; plasticated LRPC posted its highest volume and value to date. First international plasticated LRPC order for stay cable applications. Blended black and plasticated realisation about INR 79,000 per ton; management flagged some realisation softness from monsoon and project slowdowns.

segments.name: Oceanfibre (synthetic slings)
segments.commentary: Revenue has trended up for five consecutive quarters, now about GBP 2-3 million per year with a GBP 10 million target over the next few years. Gross margin 65-70%; estimated TAM INR 1.5-2 billion.

guidance_outlook: Rope volume growth of 10-12% and value growth of about 15% for FY27, conditional on the Middle East situation not worsening; management said it expects the same growth pace in coming years.
EBITDA margin floor of 20%, with quarterly variation within 20-21% and upside from capacity and mix; no margin-per-ton guidance.
Plasticated LRPC FY27 volume target of 3,500-4,000 tons against 6,000 tons annual capacity, versus about 2,500 tons in FY26.
FY27 capex of INR 250-300 crore, which management said is also the annual run-rate needed for 10-12% volume and about 15% value growth.
Thailand and UM Cables plan to be defined within 2-3 quarters; management is evaluating integrating Thailand with India operations.
capex_capacity: Elevator rope capacity expansion of about 6,000 metric tons per annum, commissioning in phases from October 2026, completion by Q1 FY28.
Furnace modernisation and expansion to meet higher demand.
Plasticated LRPC: front-end capacity exists for 6,000 tons; only the plastification line needs additional capex, and management is considering further expansion within 18-24 months.
Management said elevator rope is capacity constrained in India, with the market growing about 20%.
demand_pricing: Middle East volumes fell about 28% (roughly 1,000 tons in the quarter per management) due to the conflict, with project delays in Saudi Arabia and conservative distributor stocking; the region is about 9% of revenue.
Asia Pacific saw project-related delays, which management described as deferred rather than lost demand.
Europe contributed about 27% of revenue, and the US/Americas about 9-10%; US market share is below 5% and Europe about 10-12%.

Steel prices rose about INR 7,000 per ton (about 13% QoQ); wire rod prices were about 7% higher YoY and zinc about 28% higher. Management said 100% of commodity input increases have been passed through.
Realisations: domestic rope about INR 1,90,000 per ton; international rope INR 3,70,000-3,80,000 per ton (mix-dependent).

qa_highlights.question: How much volume loss came from the Middle East, and what is the outlook for rope volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rope volumes were marginally lower, with Middle East down about 28% and Asia Pacific seeing project delays. It reiterated 10-12% volume growth for FY27, conditional on the global situation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and how much did LRPC pricing affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management set a minimum 20% margin base, with quarterly variation in a 20-21% range from product and geographic mix. It said all steel, gas and input cost increases were passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per ton rise only about 3% QoQ when steel rose about 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the steel increase is about INR 7,000 per ton in absolute terms and is recovered in full; it is not a percentage applied to finished-product prices. EBITDA per ton was INR 40,581.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Oceanfibre TAM and why are margins high?
qa_highlights.answer: The TAM is estimated at INR 1.5-2 billion and gross margins are 65-70%. The products are specialised heavy-lifting slings for oil, offshore and wind, where steel rope cannot be used, and they need approvals and track record.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plasticated LRPC volume outlook and approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: A major domestic-share customer approval was verbally confirmed with paperwork pending. FY27 target is 3,500-4,000 tons against 2,500 tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for UM Cables and Thailand, which are loss-making?
qa_highlights.answer: UM Cables is non-core and may be repurposed for value-added wire and rope; management does not want to remain in cables long term. Thailand margins improved and a plan is expected within 6 months, possibly integrating it with India.

517206|2026-03.headline: Lumax FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR 4,184 crore with EBITDA margin at 9.8%; management guides FY27 margin 10.5-11%.
517206|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total operating revenue grew 30% y-o-y to INR 1,200 crore, with EBITDA of INR 124.9 crore (10.4% margin, 90 bps forex drag) and PAT of INR 54.1 crore. For FY26, revenue rose 23% to INR 4,184 crore, EBITDA rose 42.8% to INR 412.1 crore at a 9.8% margin, and PAT rose 23.3% to INR 172.5 crore after a one-time INR 17.8 crore labour code charge. Management flagged input cost inflation (raw materials, manpower, energy) and a roughly one-quarter pass-through lag, which it is trying to shorten through monthly price amendments with some OEMs. Order book stands at INR 2,200 crore, 88% LED.

qa_highlights.answer: Haryana revised minimum wages from 1 April 2026, with similar moves in other states. Management estimates a 30-35 bps impact and says it is passing costs to OEMs with a lag, with discussions already started.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins hold given input cost volatility and the pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise FY27 guidance given due to volatility. Full-year EBITDA margin still seen at 10.5-11%, with monthly price amendment talks underway with some OEMs to shorten the roughly one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for mould/tooling revenue?

qa_highlights.answer: FY26 turnover around INR 2,900 crore at close to 14% EBITDA margin; expected to grow with industry and keep margins; supplies 100% of Hyundai lamps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term loan INR 235 crore, of which INR 85-90 crore to be repaid in FY27; no new long-term loans planned. Short-term borrowing to rise with working capital; annual interest cost seen around INR 80 crore for FY27.

517206|2026-06.headline: Lumax Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore, with EBITDA margin flat at 9.2% as commodity recoveries slipped into Q2.
517206|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore and EBITDA rose 34% to INR 113 crore, with margin held at 9.2%, in line with Q1 FY26. PAT including associates rose 41.2% to INR 51 crore, at a 4.2% margin. Management said OEM price recoveries for West Asia-driven commodity and electronics costs were not realised in Q1 (about 150 bps margin drag) and are expected in Q2. FY27 capex guidance was raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore on new order wins.

qa_highlights.question: Why are CV and tractor orders not yet visible, and how is the company positioned on EV content?

517300|2026-06.headline: GIPCL guides FY27 EBITDA to Rs950-1,000 crore at full run-rate, anchored by 600 MW Khavda solar at 33% CUF and Rs355 crore EBITDA.
517300|2026-06.overview: Management held a post-Q4 FY26 conference call (dated 10 July 2026) covering the 600 MW Khavda solar asset, the 500 MW Khavda phase under evacuation constraints, and a planned 750 MW lignite expansion. Solar EBITDA was about Rs332 crore in FY26 and the company guided FY27 EBITDA to roughly Rs950-1,000 crore only once the 500 MW is fully operational. Interest and depreciation are set to roughly double, which compresses PBT in FY27-28. Management also flagged a 200 MW Khavda land-optimisation add and a BESS conversion at the Baroda gas site. Several answers were given as rough estimates and were not reconciled across questions.

vs Rs13 crore previous quarter; includes Rs17 crore income tax refund

segments.commentary: Commissioned December 2025 with full CTUIL allocation from November 2025; CUF 33.24% in the current quarter versus about 23% in Q4 FY26 (teething phase). Management expects 30%+ annual CUF.

segments.commentary: Advanced commissioning in phases of 200 MW, 200 MW and 100 MW, contingent on CTUIL evacuation readiness (post-monsoon, around end-2026). Rs2,065 crore CWIP sits against it.

segments.commentary: Park allotted 2,375 MW; GIPCL builds 1,100 MW itself and has sold the rest to third parties (Coal India, SJVN, SAEL). Expected net park income Rs20-25 crore a year, O&M revenue Rs50-60 crore, for 25 years.

segments.name: Gas-based stations (Baroda, ~310 MW)
segments.commentary: Idle, with no revival expected given geopolitics. Plan is to convert the site to a 120 MW BESS (GUVNL approved, tender in place), with a further 160 MW planned. Management also said it intends to hive off the gas assets from the books in the next couple of years.

517334|2026-03.headline: Motherson posted record Q4 FY26 revenue up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 42% and margin up 200 bps, and FY27 capex guided at about INR 6,000 Cr.

FY26 revenue crossed INR 1.25 Lakh Cr (+11%), EBITDA margin was 9.5%, and leverage fell to an all-time low of 0.8x. Management flagged copper up about 38% YoY and Middle East-linked crude and polymer inflation, with pass-through recovery expected to lag one or two quarters.

EBITDA rose 26% YoY with margin up 60 bps, led by the modules and polymer (MPP) business after European restructuring. Normalized PAT grew 55% YoY, with no one-off items in the quarter. Capex of INR 1,614 crore was in line with the INR 6,000 crore full-year guidance, and leverage fell to 0.8x.

517354|2026-03.headline: Havells' Q4 FY26 was modest: channel stocking for cooling hit by a mild start to summer, while cost inflation from the West Asia war drove calibrated price hikes of 5-20%.
517354|2026-03.overview: Management described a modest Q4 with cooling-product channel stocking hit by a milder start to the season, while industrial and infrastructure-linked categories stayed strong and consumer categories saw cautious trade sentiment. Cables and wires volume grew 6% YoY, with value up 14%, helped by copper and aluminium inventory gains and an approximately 8% blended price increase. Margins held except at Lloyd, which was hit by lower revenue, and a Rs 283 crore fair-value gain on the Goldi Solar investment was booked in other income. Management declined to give FY27 volume or revenue guidance, citing the uncertain war and inflation backdrop.

financial_highlights.metric: Blended cables and wires price increase
Fair value gain on Goldi Solar investment
financial_highlights.change: booked in other income in Q4

management said work in progress to restore it

segments.name: Cables and Wires
segments.commentary: Volume grew 6% YoY, with industrial cables growing much faster than domestic wires, which were flat to slightly down after destocking in the first half of Q4 against a high base. Margins rose sharply, partly from copper and aluminium inventory gains and year-end adjustments. New capacity is still running at high utilisation, and the full planned capacity is expected by end-FY26 or Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue was broadly flat YoY while contribution margin rose to 37%, which management attributed to year-end releases. The long-term margin range is 30-32%, and ASP decline has stabilised.

segments.name: Lloyd (cooling and appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 was hit by lower revenue from a delayed summer and channel inventory build; the first half of April was also slow. Price hikes of 8-15% by AC type are being implemented to pass on post-war cost increases. A new refrigerator plant at Ghiloth was commissioned in Q4.

segments.name: Fans and ECD
segments.commentary: Fans degrew in value for the full year, with Q4 hit by BEE-norm pre-stocking in Q3 and seasonality. Management expects better volumes in Q1 FY27 on a low base.

segments.name: Other (Solar)
segments.commentary: Other segment grew about 48% YoY, mainly from solar, and its EBIT margin expanded. Management called solar a sunrise industry and said margins should keep improving with operating leverage, but gave no target.

segments.name: Switchgear
segments.commentary: Contribution margin fell below the roughly 38% level because price increases lagged cost increases. Management said it is striving to return to 38% while balancing market share.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 volume or revenue growth guidance; management said it is too early given month-to-month uncertainty from the war and inflation.
Calibrated price hikes are underway across all categories, ranging from 5% to 20% by product range, with Lloyd AC hikes at 8-15%.
Management expects operating leverage in FY27, with revenue growth ahead of expense growth except advertising and promotion, which will rise by choice.
Management reiterated a medium-term EBITDA margin improvement of over 2 percentage points.
Channel inventory for Lloyd is expected to normalise by the end of April 2026 as the summer picks up in the south and west and reaches the north.
Major FY27-28 capex goes to cables and wires, about Rs 800 crore this year, plus a new R&D centre over the next 2-2.5 years. No major new Lloyd capex is planned.
capex_capacity: Cables and wires: new capacity is running at high utilisation, and the full planned capacity is expected by end-FY26 or Q1 FY27. About Rs 800 crore is budgeted this year, mainly for cables and wires.
Lloyd: a new refrigerator plant at Ghiloth was commissioned in Q4 FY26, with a refreshed product portfolio launched. No major new Lloyd capex is planned.
Solar: capacity is being built through the Goldi Solar investment (Rs 600 crore this year), and management plans to widen the renewable product range.
Underground cables are an under-invested area that the company is now investing in.
A new R&D centre will absorb a large share of capex over the next 2-2.5 years.
demand_pricing: Cooling demand was delayed by a mild start to the season. The first half of April was slow, but south and west have started well and the north is following.
Industrial and infrastructure-linked categories remained strong, while consumer categories saw cautious trade sentiment because of higher costs from West Asia disruptions.
Pricing: management said it had not seen price escalation this steep across categories in recent memory. Price increases are calibrated, and management is balancing pass-through against market share.
Pre-buying happened in March ahead of price hikes, especially in cooling products, which management said was accentuated by the price increases.
Copper prices dipped in February and then rose after the war began. Management said the entire increase seen is post-war.

Management said the company is retaining market share in all categories and denied losing share in any category. It said fans, ACs and air coolers degrew for the full year, and it does not disclose product-wise volumes.
Management said a large cement company's entry into housing wires is expected to bring consolidation and some reallocation between the unorganised and organised segments.
B2C to B2B mix has stayed at about 75:25 to 70:30, and management does not expect a meaningful shift.

qa_highlights.question: Had cables and wires volumes declined despite the 14% value growth, and was this destocking or weak end-demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew 6% YoY. Industrial cables grew much faster than domestic wires, which were flat. Wires saw destocking in the first half of Q4 against a high base from Q4 FY25 channel stocking.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins spike to 37% when revenue was flat, and does the margin normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the spike to year-end releases of dealer incentives and adjustments. The long-term average is 30-32%, and ASP decline has stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Lloyd channel inventory and sell-in/sell-out trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The first half of April was slow, and some channel inventory built up. Management expects normalised channel inventory by the end of April as summer picks up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue outlook, including a double-digit volume and price-led value growth scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, saying it is difficult to predict amid the war and inflation. It said price hikes could affect demand if they are too steep.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes fully offset raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is striving to pass on costs but must also compete and retain market share, so it will be a balancing act.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken for Lloyd and what more is needed to restore double-digit contribution margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a work in progress. Price increases of 8-15% depending on the AC type are being passed on, with post-war cost increases now flowing through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the weighted average price increase above 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said price increases range from 5% to 20% across product ranges, and it did not confirm a weighted average.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 48% growth in the Other segment, and will margins keep expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the Other growth came from solar, which benefited from capacity additions and tight supply. Management expects growth and margin improvement to continue but gave no target.

qa_highlights.question: How much cables and wires price increase was taken, and what was the volume-price split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed 6% volume growth and 14% value growth, implying a blended price increase of about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: How will fixed costs and capex change in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some investment will continue across segments in a balanced way. The company aims for revenue growth to outpace expense growth, except advertising and promotion, which will rise by choice.

risks_watch: Demand elasticity: steep price hikes across categories could slow consumer offtake, and management said it is tracking this closely.
Raw-material and forex inflation from the West Asia conflict, plus gas-supply disruptions that hit production, with only partial pass-through so far.
Lloyd returns: about Rs 4,000 crore of capital is deployed with barely any profitability, and management's turnaround depends on brand building and operating leverage.

New entrants in housing wires, including a large cement company, could add pricing pressure.
Fans and cooling Q1 FY27 volumes, which depend on the summer and monsoon, after BEE-norm stocking in Q3 FY26.
Cables and wires margins may have been boosted by one-off inventory gains and year-end adjustments, so the quarter's margin is not a run rate.

517354|2026-06.headline: Havells Q1 FY27: strong revenue growth on calibrated price hikes (7-8% average), but profitability hit by front-loaded A&P; contribution margin stable near 18.3%.
517354|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong revenue quarter with resilient demand despite raw material inflation and West Asia uncertainty. Calibrated, staggered price hikes averaging about 7-8% (range 5-20%) were taken across categories, with cables and wires seeing the largest increases. A&P spend more than doubled year-on-year, which management said front-loaded investment and weighed on quarterly profitability. Renewables is now reported as a separate segment and is growing rapidly, while switchgear sales fell about 4% YoY with margin erosion of around 260 bps. Management gave no formal FY27 guidance, but said the quarter start was positive.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was the most volatile quarter; calibrated hikes were taken with an eye on market share and channel inventory was kept lean. It believes market share was held or gained on a secondary-sales basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year A&P budget and is it a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management indicated roughly INR700-800 crore for FY27 (agreed to the 'somewhere around that number' framing). Long-term A&P is about 2.7% of revenue and will remain consistent over 4-5 years; Lloyd A&P elevated for a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Is contribution margin going to recover to double digits in Lloyd and when will margins normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Lloyd should return to double-digit contribution margin in full quarters, not in seasonally weak Q2/Q3. Normalised contribution margin for switchgear was described as roughly 37-40%, and company contribution margin is expected to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the switchgear business weaker in demand and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed West Asia shipping disruption, raw material volatility that hurt pass-through, and trade confusion; domestic demand is stable and recovery expected from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why are cable volumes flat despite capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to raw material volatility slowing sell-in, dealers selling from their own stock as copper prices fell, and a shift to sell-out distribution; it said not to judge on one quarter.

517385|2026-03.headline: Symphony FY26 consol revenue fell 28% to ₹1,131 crores; Australia fully impaired, taking PAT to negative ₹141 crores.
517385|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue fell 28% YoY to ₹1,131 crores and PBT before exceptional items fell to ₹149 crores from ₹326 crores, with PAT at negative ₹141 crores after a ₹259 crores consolidated impairment. Q4 consolidated revenue was ₹338 crores (vs ₹488 crores) and EBITDA margin fell to 15.5% from 21.2%, while gross margin held at 46.4%. Management completed a balance-sheet reset: the entire ₹348 crores Australia equity investment is impaired, no further capital will go to Australia, and the US business and Bonaire IPRs were bought into Symphony India for about ₹52 crores. Standalone Q4 revenue was ₹199 crores (vs ₹368 crores) on a high base and channel caution, with management pointing to a possible 4 to 6 week summer runway from mid-May.

517385|2026-06.headline: Symphony Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 8% to ₹378 crore; adjusted PAT up 23% to ₹43 crore, with management warning of near-term margin pressure from input costs.
517385|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 8% YoY to ₹378 crore and EBITDA reported was ₹48 crore (up 26%), but management said June 2026 included a ₹5 crore one-time non-cash charge while June 2025 had ₹9 crore of exceptional income; on that basis EBITDA was ₹53 crore vs ₹38 crore and PAT ₹43 crore vs ₹35 crore. Domestic India revenue grew 15% and modern trade grew over 100%, which management attributed largely to general trade channel inventory being cleared last year. Gross margin was 49.8% and EBITDA margin 12.6%, but management guided to short-term margin pressure from elevated commodity and plastic costs, with only partial price pass-through. Australia (CTPL) remains weak, with management committing to no further capital deployment.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales comes from modern trade and e-commerce, and how does its profitability compare with general trade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose the exact share for competitive reasons. Modern trade profitability is almost comparable to general trade.

qa_highlights.question: Will input cost inflation such as plastic hit margins in coming quarters, or will it all be passed on given low channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin pressure is expected in the short term because costs remain elevated and depend on how long the war lasts. Symphony will pass on some but not all of the increase; the impact is hard to quantify yet despite value engineering.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the modern trade growth above 100%: share gain, market growth, strategy change, or low base?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the absence of channel inventory in modern trade and e-commerce, versus general trade which carried elevated inventory from the prior year. Management said growth of this scale is unlikely to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What SKUs are driving Bonaire USA growth, and how does its distribution differ from Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: Products are rebranded Indian SKUs, led by the Air Force model, sold to Home Depot and Lowe's, aided by a hot Southwest US summer. Bonaire uses a US warehouse and retailer model, whereas Australia sells mostly to installation companies, with retail still small.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give revenue, EBITDA and PAT for all subsidiaries?

qa_highlights.question: What price hikes have been taken and what is planned, given raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: No price hike yet in the household cooler segment. Outside household coolers, 7% to 10% hikes have been taken, with more planned in coming days; the extent depends on when the war ends and costs normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy to turn around CTPL Australia?
qa_highlights.answer: No additional capital will be deployed; the impairment and write-off is treated as history from FY26. Management said there is nothing new on product, distribution or manufacturing beyond what is already in place.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BISP product categories beyond exports, and are tabletop fans and water heaters sold online or offline?
qa_highlights.answer: BISP includes large-space ventilated air coolers, tabletop fans (sold year-round), water heaters and exports. Management said these are already in modern retail and GT in top cities, but not yet nationwide. BISP is about 48% of consol revenue and 23% of standalone TTM revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there demand for air coolers in the US, a developed market with high per-capita income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said coolers are not seen as a poor man's AC outside India and are sold in the US, Europe and the Middle East. In the US they are used outdoors, as whole-house or window-mounted units in the dry Southwest, and their key advantage is portability and plug-and-play use.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Mexico and USA sales, given the summer conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Mexico had two consecutive mild summers (2025 and 2026), so management expects significant growth in summer 2027 if conditions are normal or robust, without giving a number. USA sales should also rise next summer if the summer is similarly good.

qa_highlights.question: Have export shipments resumed, and are geopolitical issues affecting orders?

517498|2026-03.headline: Websol FY26 revenue rose 82% to INR 1,049 crore and PAT 96% to INR 303 crore, with Q4 revenue of INR 401 crore and a INR 1,161 crore order book.

The company turned net cash surplus, cash from operations was INR 255 crore, and cell capacity doubled to ~1.2 GW after cell line 2 commissioning in September 2025. Management plans to upgrade one 600 MW Mono PERC line to TOPCon (capacity to 1.35 GW) by February 2027, while Andhra Pradesh expansion timing remains undisclosed beyond a June 2027 target. Margin compression was attributed to a higher module mix, silver costs and softer cell and module realisations.

517506|2026-03.headline: TTK Prestige Q4 FY26 domestic revenue grew 14.4% and company revenue 12.5%, with operating EBITDA of INR81.7 crore, up 43.8%.
517506|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was driven by domestic demand, with induction cooktops giving a short-term boost to appliances, and exports constrained by supply chain disruption. Operating EBITDA rose 43.8% to INR81.7 crore and PBT rose 35.9% to INR71.9 crore, though exceptional charges relating to the new Labour Code were incurred. Gross margin expanded despite commodity inflation, which management attributed mainly to inventory management and mix, with the mid-quarter price hike only partly visible. For FY26, company revenue grew 9.6% (domestic 9.8%), operating EBITDA grew 12% and PAT rose about 14% to INR185 crore. Management flagged input cost inflation of about 10% post the West Asia conflict and expects margins to dip during the ongoing investment phase.

Cookers industry mix is about 50-55% stainless steel versus about 45% aluminium. Kitchenware plants run at 85%+ utilisation.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Appliances grew about 10% in FY26 per management, with Q4 lifted by induction cooktop demand driven by a replacement shift during the volatile quarter. Appliance plants run at about 75-80% utilisation; the partner-manufactured model is treated as hybrid in-sourcing.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were a drag in Q4 due to disrupted global supply chains, despite order inflow. Management says the business is maintained, prior growth was 20-22% on a small base, and the domestic market is the priority.

segments.name: Prestige Exclusive stores
segments.commentary: Contribute about 12-15% of business and are growing in double digits; about 700+ stores and about 100 new stores opened. Management described them as a significant growth driver.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin or revenue guidance given; management declined to guide on profitability.

qa_highlights.question: How much of appliance growth of about 20% is from induction cooktops, and will momentum continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not quantify the induction contribution but said appliances grew reasonably even excluding it. Some trend continues into Q1, and induction adoption may last a couple more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the input cost inflation currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Average input cost increase of about 10%, with some areas up about 15%, post the war scenario. Price hikes are inevitable, weighed against demand.

qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore over 3 years started Q4 FY25, to continue for a few more quarters and taking forms beyond consultants. Management did not give a split for FY26 or FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: General trade growth is attributed to company-specific initiatives on distribution and hygiene. Management said new entrants compete on price and D2C, but the category is growing enough to absorb it; Judge is played separately in the mass segment, and its margins were not compared.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide FY27 ad budget and FY26 amount, saying normally 5-6% of sales is spent on advertising, sales and promotion.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin recover, and is it to pre-investment levels?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects a dip in EBITDA margin during the investment phase lasting about 2 more years, then a return to the earlier 13-14% margin as investments yield results.

qa_highlights.question: Did GST-related channel filling shift growth from Q3 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said channel inventory is normalised and GST had little impact on Q4 performance.

517506|2026-09.headline: TTK Prestige Q2 FY27: revenue up about 21.9% with domestic up 23.4% and operating EBITDA up about 70.9%, but cost inflation is set to pressure gross margin.
517506|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, with top-line growth backed by consumer demand, premiumization, and new product launches. Domestic sales grew about 23.4% and operating EBITDA about 70.9%, per management's remarks on the call. Input cost inflation across roughly 95% of input line items is the main concern, and management said price increases have been staggered and only partly absorbed. Two exceptional items were booked this quarter: the exit from the 51% subsidiary Ultra Fresh Modular Solution and a loss of about Rs 2 crore on a compulsory convertible debenture in a rural distribution startup that shut down.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 18 crore in Q2 FY26 strategic expenses, which did not recur

financial_highlights.value: Ultra Fresh investment exit (amount not stated) and Rs 2 crore CCD write-off

segments.name: Cookers
segments.commentary: Around 30-32% of revenue per management's breakdown in the investor presentation.

segments.name: Cookware
segments.commentary: Around 15-18% of revenue. Tri-ply is growing about 1.5 times the industry average, and enamel cookware is an early new launch.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Close to 50% of revenue. Appliances are outsourced to exclusive partners. Induction is growing faster than the company, with management guiding to high-teens growth for the category.

guidance_outlook: Cost inflation is expected to keep flowing through the next few quarters, with more price increases needed; management said recovery through price is difficult and gross margin pressure will start to show.
Soft expense plan is Rs 200-250 crore over three years, with about Rs 100 crore spent over the last six to eight quarters and about Rs 150 crore still to be spent over the remaining year.
Management reiterated a 13-14% EBITDA margin band but said it will be cautious given cost volatility.
Some festive-season sales are expected to flow into Q3 FY27.
Industry growth outlook is high-teens for the category, with management calling growth sustainable though less dramatic than recent quarters.
capex_capacity: Ultra Fresh Modular Solution (51% subsidiary) investment exited; management said the focus is the core categories and markets.
Strategic spend is shifting from capability building toward brand and innovation in the next few quarters.
Ninety percent of kitchenware is manufactured in-house; appliances are outsourced to exclusive partners.
Tri-ply cookware inputs are partly sourced from China (no domestic source cited).
demand_pricing: Industry demand is recovering after a lull, supported by urban premiumization, kitchen modernization, and migration from unorganized to organized players due to cost pressure.
Price increases were taken in a step jump but staggered; management said the industry has not fully absorbed the cost increase.
Commodity inputs (aluminium, stainless steel, rubber, chemicals, packaging) are up, with current prices above Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 levels, and old-cost inventory is now used up.
E-commerce plus quick commerce is about 20% of sales; growth is described as even across channels.
Competition is mainly from digital-first brands in cookware, and management has not yet seen their impact on growth.
Judge brand is positioned lower in the mass market, with a structurally lower margin than Prestige; management declined to quantify the gap.

qa_highlights.question: Which commodities are driving cost increases, and are competitors taking price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 95% of input line items are affected, including packaging, handles, rubber and chemicals. Price increases were taken in a staggered manner and the industry has not fully absorbed the costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much soft expense has been spent and how much is budgeted?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 85-100 crore was spent last year and Rs 13 crore in H1 FY27. The plan is Rs 200-250 crore over three years, and spend is being realigned toward brand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory build and why did cash flow come under pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the build reflects demand anticipation and manufacturing changes, and that inventory days have not risen; the absolute value is higher because of the growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost pressure in RM and will pricing continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs are still above Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 levels. Management said old-cost inventory benefits are used up, so pressure will reach gross margin, and more price action is possible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Judge brand cannibalizing Prestige, and what is its margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cannibalization is minimal because the brands target different segments. Judge is positioned at the lower end of the mass market with a slightly lower margin than Prestige, but no figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 FY26 included about Rs 18 crore of strategic expenses that did not recur, and cost optimization benefits are flowing through. More strategic spend is planned.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from RM inflation, with management saying price increases may not fully offset costs.
Demand elasticity if price increases continue, which management flagged as a concern.
Competition from digital-first cookware brands, whose impact is not yet visible.
Soft expense spend of about Rs 150 crore still to come, which could weigh on EBITDA.
Inventory build straining cash flow, with the absolute level higher despite stable inventory days.
Export business under pressure from geopolitical and UK/Europe macro conditions.

517522|2026-03.headline: Rajratan Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin dipped on a ~INR10,000/ton steel price spike it could not pass on; FY26 sales volume up 18% to over 133,000 tons.
517522|2026-03.overview: Management reported record sales tonnage for FY26 of more than 133,000 tons, up 18% YoY, from three locations (India, Thailand, and the newly merged USA subsidiary). Q4 EBITDA margin fell because steel wire rod rose by almost INR10,000/ton from January to March, which could not be passed on, while energy availability and cost also weighed. Management said the price increases have been passed on from April and expects margins to recover to 13-13.5% in Q1 FY27, with a sustained consolidated band of 13.5-14%. FY27 volume growth target is 17-18%, with Chennai capacity doubling to 60,000 tons by Q2 and steel cord (conveyor belt) trials starting in Q2.

EBITDA margin impact from unpassed raw material cost

segments.commentary: Europe to grow about 50% from a low base; Southeast Asia to grow 10-15%. Japan is an early new opportunity.

Competition: capacity exceeds demand, some global players may not survive, and new entrants must price lower; management says Rajratan's realisation is at the higher end.
Management expects the auto slowdown has not yet hit but expects a possible slowdown in April-May; this is not confirmed in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 13-14% and can they be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 dip was from the Jan-Mar steel spike, now passed on from April; margin expected to return to 13-13.5% in Q1 FY27, and 13.5-14% is the sustainable consolidated band.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: A new consolidated USA subsidiary (Rajratan USA) is now merged; about INR30 crore of FOB shipping and logistics cost for the second half is booked there, not in Thailand. This could rise with export volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate low in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Thailand BOI privilege: income tax is exempt beyond 36,000 tons of sales, giving an effective rate of about 13.9% on the privileged company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is seeking a change in the PLI ladder after missing the year 1 and year 2 production targets; without approval, no PLI is assumed. If approved, it is 8% of incremental sales, about INR40-50 crore over 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the steel cord/wire rope business and what is its economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel cord for conveyor belts; 10,000 tons/year capacity, about INR150 crore peak revenue at about INR150/kg, reached in about two years (FY29), current EBITDA margin about 20%. Management says it is a pilot and not a big investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand Chennai when margins and pricing are under pressure?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Gains from FX: the USD appreciated against the rupee on larger exports, and the Thai Baht strengthened, reflected in the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Thailand and USA combined EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Thailand Q4 EBITDA margin was 10% (corrected from 7.5% on the call). Management said Thailand and USA business had no substantial change and said it would respond separately on the combined figure.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility: wire rod rose about INR10,000/ton in Jan-Mar, and the company could not pass on costs immediately; margin depends on price pass-through.
Working capital and debt: export credit cycles of 45-60 days plus US duty costs push up working capital; management expects borrowing to stay at about 7-7.5% and not reduce.

517569|2026-03.headline: KEI Q4 FY26 net sales rose 19.3% to INR3,476 crores and PAT 25.5% to INR284 crores; management guides 17-18% FY27 volume growth.

For FY26, net sales reached INR11,746 crores (up 20.66%), EBITDA INR1,387 crores (11.81% margin) and PAT INR918 crores. Q4 volume growth was only about 2%, which management attributed to capacity constraints, with Sanand plant sales under INR100 crores in the quarter. Middle East shipping disruption in March cost an estimated INR50-60 crores of exports, and April freight costs are being shared with customers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the remaining net cash will be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev said INR500-600 crores of cash will be held at all times for operations; the balance above that can fluctuate with working capital needs.

517569|2026-06.headline: KEI Industries Q1 FY27 net sales rose 23% to INR3,185 crore and operating margin reached 12.43%, with EBITDA up 39.5%.

Operating (EBITDA) margin expanded to 13.04% from 11.49%, and PAT rose 40% to INR274 crore, helped by product mix (EHV, retail/dealer channel) and operating leverage. Exports fell to INR341 crore from INR375 crore because Middle East orders were not executed and US custom duty issues persisted. Management reiterated a 20%+ growth target, though it declined to raise guidance above that, and said the Sanand plant is ramping up slowly.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex grow slowly and what drove the sharp wire and cable margin rise from 12.4% to 13.6% quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said fixed costs did not rise with incremental sales, and product mix and export margin orders helped. He said the company has crossed its earlier sub-11% operating margin hurdle and expects 11-12% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing market share given industry volume growth near 33-35%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied losing share, citing strong demand and capacity constraints. It reiterated a 20%+ CAGR target and said it is not chasing 35-40% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sanand revenue guidance for FY27 and the capacity potential?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said FY27 Sanand revenue of INR1,500-2,000 crore, correcting a media figure of about INR3,000 crore. Management said the long-run potential is INR6,000 crore, rising to about INR7,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 20%+ guidance not raised given industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited capital allocation discipline, the need to fund capex for future capacity, and working capital limits. It said actual growth could exceed guidance but it would not give higher numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports fall and can they grow about 50% over the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said Middle East shipments were blocked and US orders stalled; shipments have resumed at high freight cost. He expects exports to grow to meet the 17-18% share target.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the house wire breakup dropped and what is the outlook for retail share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give product-wise sales because competitors use the data. It said retail is favoured for lower working capital needs, and the mix may shift with export orders.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margin was unrepresentative because of inventory valuation, with the effects averaging out over H1, and that the 11% EBITDA guidance is on an annualised basis. It said H1 operating margin was 11.09% against 10.27-11% over five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11% margin guidance a cut from the earlier 11-12% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no cut: 11% is the FY27 level, moving to 11-11.5% and then 11.5-12% as Sanand ramps up, with the 11-12% range completing across FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 revenue growth stronger than the usual 20-25% range, and does this imply a slower H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it guides to 25%-plus conservatively to avoid missing guidance. It said H1 growth of about 30-31% already exceeds that guidance, and that the company will add more growth where capital allows.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports and the US order book support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export sales were flat at INR 493 crores (vs INR 472 crores), and the export order book is INR 991 crores with the USA at about 50%. It expects export growth to pick up in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in inventory and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than INR 600-700 crores of the inventory build is at Sanand, with the balance from copper valuation at the existing plants. It expects inventory to normalise to about 90 days of COGS by March 2027, and said debtor days have already fallen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EHV revenue opportunity after Sanand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sanand adds INR 1,500-1,700 crores of new EHV capacity in value terms on top of existing EHV sales of about INR 700 crores, with peak Sanand revenue in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth is volume versus value, and what is the capital constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is guided in value terms because budgets are set in value and working capital limits growth to about 25-30%. It said a 16-17% volume growth with 50% price growth would imply a 67-70% value increase, which it considers unfeasible.

519126|2026-03.headline: HFL posted record FY26 PAT of INR149 crores (+29% YoY) and guides FY27 PAT of INR200-220 crores, while cash flow lagged on working capital.

Management reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores but moved the GST inversion-driven shift from gross to net revenue recognition to Q2-Q3 FY27, and withheld sales and segment profitability guidance.
