So EBITDA margins will always remain between 11% to 13%. Once our polymer gets on stream by December 2027, in the next year we will like to give you a band of 14% to 16%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Margin guided at 11-13% until polymer is on stream, then 14-16% once polymer Phase 1 (INR78 crore, 66,500 t captive) commissions Jun-Dec 2027; Q2 EBITDA margin was 12.9% and management says margin rose ~240 bps, though part of that is falling metal prices lifting percentage margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Copper cable line already live at 1,500 t/month and being scaled to 2,500 t/month; LV cable project due before April 2027; polymer Phase 1 commissioning Jun-Dec 2027 and Phase 2 early 2028; capacity utilisation at about 45% of target once balancing equipment is operational.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR4,300-4,500 crore held, implying ~INR2,580 crore in H2 versus INR1,722 crore in H1 (about 50% step-up); firm order book INR3,735 crore (book-to-bill 1.29x) and ~INR750 crore data-centre revenue expected in FY27, though the H2 step-up is large.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only ~45% of target, but a 2028-2032 capacity roadmap (about five new MV lines a year from 2028) is to be shared at end Q4 FY27, and the solar cable plant (1,000 km/month) is planned within 18 months, with polymer Phase 2 (INR92 crore) also planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue guidance at INR4,300-4,500 crore rather than raising it, and H1 revenue is INR1,722 crore, so an upgrade would need H2 to clearly exceed the INR2,580 crore implied.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must deliver about INR2,580 crore (50% above H1) and depends on Q3-Q4 order inflow (INR350-400 crore/month) and the seasonal tender cycle; polymer delays would defer the 14-16% margin target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sixth CCV line due within one year, solar 3.3 kV single-core cable plant planned within 18 months, and export products (UL approval applied for US MV cables; large export contribution expected in FY28).

rows.label: Order book converts to revenue by March 2027
rows.why: Management targets about INR2,500 crore of execution from the ~INR4,300 crore order book at market prices by March 2027, with H1 inflow of INR2,217 crore and monthly inflow of INR350-400 crore.

rows.label: EHV share to double digit in Q3/Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management targets EHV revenue at double-digit share of top line in Q3 and Q4 FY27, supported by INR974 crore AL59 800 kV HVDC order and ~INR32,000 crore of live MV/EHV enquiries expected to finalise within 90 days.

rows.label: Legacy receivable recovery
rows.why: Legacy receivables are INR957 crore with a target of INR300 crore recovered within 24 months, but only INR116 crore is customer-confirmed so far.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance, data centre demand and the polymer-driven margin path, but cautious on FY28 capacity, the 2028-2032 roadmap and the Adani concentration (43% of order book); analysts pressed on margin sustainability and metal-price effects.

522195|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 39.22% to ₹322.06 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 26.80%, with management guiding ~30% growth to ₹500 crore gross revenue in FY27.
522195|2026-03.overview: Frontier Springs delivered FY26 revenue from operations of ₹322.06 crore (up 39.22%), EBITDA of ₹86.31 crore (up 73.80%) and PAT of ₹61.31 crore (up 76.88%). Q4 revenue was ₹82.54 crore (up 17.7% YoY, marginally above Q3) with EBITDA margin of 28.51%. Management guides FY27 gross revenue above ₹500 crore on an order book it put at ₹300-370 crore, and says it expects to hold margins at 23-24% or higher, while acknowledging steel-cost pressure could trim 1-2 points. Q&A centred on margin guidance, the FIBA product launch, air spring capacity and wagon tenders.

financial_highlights.change: up 17.7% YoY; marginally ahead of Q3 FY26
margin up 362 bps QoQ-stated as YoY in call and 462 bps YoY in call; call states both 362 bps and 462 bps

segments.name: Coil springs
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited by management as approximately ₹175 crore plus (analyst's recollection, confirmed as approximate gross figure). Management expects reasonable growth in FY27.

segments.name: Forging
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited as ₹60 crore plus. A new 6-ton hammer was installed; it currently runs one 8-hour shift against 16 hours of available capacity. Management expects the strongest growth here in FY27.

segments.name: Air springs (coach sets)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited as approximately ₹150 crore. Capacity is 300 coach sets per month; output is 180-200 per month. Realisation cited at about ₹1.25 lakh per air spring, described as slightly improved.

segments.name: FIBA (failure indication and brake application system)
segments.commentary: New product with RDSO basic approval and patent done; trials on trains start now, with about 6 months to regular supply. Management sizes the market at ₹40-50 crore and expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28. Margin said to be similar to air and coil springs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross revenue target above ₹500 crore, described as around 30% growth, backed by an order book of ₹300-370 crore disclosed on the call.
Margin target of 23-24% for the year, with management saying 26-28% is possible; management conceded 1-2 points could be lost on existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Medium-term growth of 25% per year beyond FY27 was stated; management also said 20-25% average growth is achievable across the three product lines.
FY27 capex planned at ₹20-25 crore across all three divisions, after about ₹20 crore in FY26; no term loans taken in several years.

Q4 FY27 is expected to be the strongest quarter, with the 6-ton hammer contributing from the third quarter onward; management expects the first-half revenue run-rate to break out of the ₹80-83 crore band.
capex_capacity: Air spring capacity 300 coach sets per month, utilisation 180-200 per month (about 60-67%); final testing is the bottleneck, and two more testing machines are planned.
Overall plant utilisation about 70% per management; a new automated coil spring line from China is under negotiation.
A 6-ton forging hammer was installed in FY26, joining 1-ton and 3-ton hammers; utilisation is one 8-hour shift out of 16 hours available.
FY27 capex of ₹20-25 crore across coil, air and forging divisions, focused on capacity and less manpower-intensive automation.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is ₹300-370 crore, mostly Railways. Orders come in daily, mainly small, and are not individually disclosed; the company agreed to post larger orders on the exchanges.
Railways' fixed-price contracts limit mid-contract price increases. Management is raising prices in new tenders to pass through steel and energy cost increases.
Railways' production plan for FY27 is about 6,000 passenger coaches and 1,200-1,400 locomotives, flat YoY; a large wagon tender is expected, with forging and springs supply.
Competition: no new spring or forging players, though more steel suppliers have been added by Railways, improving sourcing terms.
Q3 FY26 revenue was flagged as constrained by inspection delays, raw material delays and customer-side bottlenecks; the company is targeting a breakout above ₹82-83 crore per quarter.
Export: management said coil spring exports are not being pursued; forging exports to Europe and the US are being explored where margins are good.
Defence and non-rail forging (L&T, JCB, Caterpillar, cranes) are at sample or R&D stage; defence approvals are slow.

qa_highlights.question: What margin should be expected if steel prices stay high: 22-23% or 26-27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 23-24% for FY27 'if not 26-28%', citing negotiations with steel and energy suppliers and price increases in future tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between pass-through of commodity costs and the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing tenders at fixed prices may be lower; if the year completes, margin could fall by 1-2 points, but management aims to hold current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility for FY28-29 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific figure yet; management sees no order scarcity for 5-10 years and said growth of 25% is expected beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of FY26 revenue by division and air spring capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate gross figures: coil springs ₹175 crore plus, forging ₹60 crore plus, air springs ₹150 crore; air spring output 180-190 coach sets per month against 300 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue been stuck at ₹80-83 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Bottlenecks include delayed inspections by Railways inspectors and occasional raw material delays; management expects to break out in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FIBA opportunity and its FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Market of ₹40-50 crore; company is second indigenous source after imports, with 2-3 approved sources in total. Management expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28 once trials conclude.

risks_watch: Steel and energy costs: management concedes margin may fall 1-2 points on fixed-price existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Quarterly revenue has been stuck at ₹80-83 crore for three quarters; the FY27 ₹500 crore target depends on a sharp step-up.
Receivables are high at year end; management attributes this to high turnover and says there are zero bad debts. Next quarter's collections should be checked.
Timing of the large wagon tender and the FIBA trial and approval, both of which are needed for the second-half ramp-up.
Air spring testing bottleneck and whether two more testing machines are commissioned in time.
Defence and non-rail forging diversification is still at sample stage.
522195|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand and growth, but notably hedged on margins ('if not 26-28%', 'I am a little conservative'). Responses on the wagon tender, FIBA timing and quarterly revenue breakout were more forward-looking than backed by numbers.
key_quotes: We enter FY26 with an order book of X300 crores which gives us good revenue visibility over guidance for FY26 as it crosses X500 crores in gross revenues to step up over 30% from what we delivered in FY26.
Financial Year 26 was a year where frontier Spring demonstrated that it can grow revenues at ascale, expand margins and simultaneously invest in future capacity all at the same time.
There are zero bad debts in the company.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets 23-24% EBITDA margin for FY27 versus 26.80% in FY26, with 26-28% 'if not' and 1-2 points at risk from fixed-price tenders if steel stays firm, so the call points to compression rather than expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Air spring output is 180-200 per month against 300 capacity (about 60-67%), so the constraint is final testing, not floor capacity; two more testing machines are planned, and the new China coil line is only under negotiation.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 gross revenue guided above ₹500 crore (~30% growth on ~₹385 crore FY26 gross), backed by a ₹300-370 crore order book, but quarterly revenue has been stuck at ₹80-83 crore for three quarters so the step-up is back-ended.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Plant utilisation is about 70%, FY27 capex is guided at ₹20-25 crore, and a new automated coil spring line from China is under negotiation, so a formal capex announcement is likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is hedged on margins ('I am a little conservative', 23-24% if not 26-28%) and the revenue step-up has not yet shown in three quarters at ₹80-83 crore, so an upgrade in the window looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Quarterly revenue has been flat at ₹80-83 crore for three quarters against a ~₹500 crore FY27 target, and margin could fall 1-2 points on fixed-price tenders if steel stays firm.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: FIBA has RDSO basic approval and patent done, trials start now with about 6 months to regular supply, and management expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28 against a ₹40-50 crore market.

rows.label: Wagon tender and ₹300-370 crore order book
rows.why: Order book of ₹300-370 crore is mostly Railways and a large wagon tender is expected with forging and springs supply, but timing is not confirmed and the company does not disclose individual orders.

rows.label: 6-ton hammer ramp-up in forging
rows.why: The 6-ton hammer runs one 8-hour shift against 16 hours available, and management expects forging to grow fastest in FY27 with contribution from Q3 onward.

rows.label: Year-end receivables high
rows.why: Management attributes high year-end receivables to high turnover and claims zero bad debts, but next quarter's collections are unverified.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the ₹500 crore FY27 target and the 6-ton hammer, but hedged on margins ('if not 26-28%', 'a little conservative'); analysts pressed on margin guidance, the FIBA launch, air spring capacity and the wagon tender.

522205|2026-03.headline: Praj Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT before exceptionals fell to Rs 15.4 mn from Rs 582.5 mn; Q4 order intake Rs 6,580 mn, backlog Rs 43,050 mn.
522205|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 8,445 mn versus Rs 8,598 mn a year earlier, while PAT fell to Rs 116 mn from Rs 398 mn. FY26 revenue was Rs 31,679 mn (vs Rs 32,280 mn) and PAT was Rs 238 mn (vs Rs 289 mn). Management attributed margin pressure mainly to site execution cost escalation on delayed projects, continued investment in Praj GenX, and non-business one-time items, rather than raw material prices. Order intake was weak, with several engineering and GenX inquiries (about Rs 300 mn+ inquiry basket) deferred on raw material price uncertainty.

segments.commentary: 67% of FY26 revenue and 86% of Q4 order intake; 78% of backlog. Greenfield 1G fuel ethanol demand slowed, with smaller brownfield, DCO co-product and ENA greenfield orders partly offsetting.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: 22% of FY26 revenue; 2% of Q4 order intake and 16% of backlog. Several opportunities deferred from Q4 on raw material uncertainty, now expected to reflect in FY27.

segments.name: PHS (ZLD/PHS businesses)
segments.commentary: 11% of FY26 revenue; 12% of Q4 order intake and 5% of backlog. One joint order closed with a semiconductor company in the current quarter.

segments.commentary: Fixed overhead run rate about Rs 10 crore per month. Data centre modular cooling order (Rs 50-150 crore range by size) under final negotiation, expected in Q1 FY27.

Ordering expected to return to a Rs 800-900 crore band on a steady-state basis (management said this is a ballpark, not guidance).
First bio-IBA order expected in Q1 FY27.
GenX break-even targeted in FY27, contingent on booking orders over the next two to three quarters.
Management believes execution challenges are largely resolved and FY27 focus is operational excellence; 'to a great extent the worst is over'.
Blending mandates expected within about one year per management; E22/E25/E27/E30 BIS fuel specifications now notified.
capex_capacity: Praj GenX facility (Mangalore) is large and sophisticated; utilisation expected to rise with data centre and LNG/oil and gas orders.
Client certifications for the Mangalore facility rose to about 12-13 clients from about nine at end of Q3 FY26.
CBG capacity ramp-up underway at a few plants using Napier grass and rice straw mixed feedstock.
R&D spend in FY26 about Rs 65-66 crore, of which about Rs 20 crore capex (lab and equipment) and about Rs 45-46 crore opex (in other expenses).
Basic engineering order for one ethanol-to-SAF plant for an international customer being completed; detailed engineering order under discussion.
demand_pricing: Q4 raw material costs rose about 3% on a consolidated basis, offset partly by a 2% fall in other expenses; net margin impact about 1-1.5%. Management said the larger pressure was site-related execution cost escalation.
YTD raw material prices broadly flat per management; contracting has moved from 100% fixed-price to some flexibility on raw material price changes.
About Rs 300 mn+ of inquiries deferred from Q4 due to raw material price and supply chain uncertainty.
Government roadmap: 150 E85/E100 outlets in Delhi, Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur within a month, 500 within 6-12 months, and 5,000 E100 stations within 24 months.
Export revenues were 36% of FY26 revenue. Positive biofuel policy signals in the US (15% ethanol blend bill passed by House), Indonesia, Vietnam, Kenya, Latin America and others.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins and profits declined over three years despite R&D investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBP-20 capacity build-out ended, reducing greenfield ethanol plant orders, while GenX investment over 2.5-3 years held back profits; order books are expected to benefit in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much did raw material inflation hit Q4 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said raw material costs rose about 3% in Q4 with other expenses down 2%, net impact 1-1.5%; the main driver was site execution cost escalation linked to project delays. YTD raw material costs were broadly flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deferred order quantum and GenX outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Deferred inquiries were about Rs 300 mn+ (called an inquiry basket, not orders). GenX data centre order ranges Rs 50-150 crore; GenX fixed overhead run rate about Rs 10 crore per month; break-even targeted in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for mandates beyond E20 and what is the ethanol capacity impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mandates likely within one year. Blends of 2-5% could be met by existing capacity with efficiency gains; above 5% needs new capacity, which Praj is ready to supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected steady-state order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline supports a Rs 800-900 crore range typically, but stopped short of formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are the R&D spend and the synergy between bioenergy and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 R&D about Rs 65-66 crore (about Rs 20 crore capex, Rs 45-46 crore opex, about 100 scientists). Data centre work is cooling skids and modules; long term, bioenergy could power medium and large data centres.

risks_watch: Execution cost escalation and open sites; management says challenges are resolved but Q4 PBT was only Rs 15.4 mn.
Raw material and supply chain volatility on fixed-price contracts, with deferred inquiries pending price visibility.

Conversion of GenX data centre order expected in Q1 FY27 and bio-IBA first order in Q1 FY27.
Greenfield 1G ethanol slowdown and funding delays extending project execution cycles.
Leadership restructuring with the MD and JMD/CFO roles; a shareholder asked about buyback and bonus options (Board matter).

key_quotes: Overall impact is 1 -1.5% additional which we have incurred.

We believe that it will be not longer than one year, but really to predict it in terms of exact months is difficult for us.

rows.why: Backlog of Rs 43,050 mn gives revenue cover, but Q4 revenue fell about 2% to Rs 8,445 mn and order intake of Rs 6,580 mn was weak; management's Rs 800-900 crore ordering band is explicitly not guidance and Rs 300 mn+ inquiries are deferred.

rows.why: No board capex plan was stated and utilisation was not disclosed; the brief has no capacity-utilisation figure, and order intake of Rs 6,580 mn in Q4 is weak, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The first bio-IBA order and the data-centre modular cooling order (Rs 50-150 crore per order) are expected in Q1 FY27, but these are orders on existing offerings rather than launches, and timing depends on negotiations.

rows.why: About Rs 300 mn+ of inquiries were deferred on raw material price uncertainty, and management says engineering opportunities are now expected to reflect in FY27, but conversion depends on price visibility.

522205|2026-06.headline: Praj Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 116.1 mn (vs INR 53.4 mn) on INR 7.16 bn revenue, with order intake of INR 10 bn and backlog of INR 45.9 bn.
522205|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations rose to INR 7.16 bn from INR 6.4 bn a year earlier, and PBT before exceptional items more than doubled to INR 210.5 mn. Order intake was INR 10 bn, with 57% domestic, and backlog stood at INR 45.9 bn at June 30, 2026. Management said execution remains slowed by first-generation ethanol funding issues and supply-demand imbalance, while new verticals (Praj GenX data-center work, Bio-IBA demo plant, Brazil corn-to-ethanol plant, ZLD/HiPurity for semiconductors) are starting to show orders. Margins were described as subdued on volume and mix, and management declined to give margin guidance.

segments.name: Bioenergy
segments.commentary: 66% of revenue and 62% of order intake; bioenergy revenue cited at INR 474 crore in the quarter. Domestic first-gen ethanol greenfield slowed; brownfield, DCO and ENA demand holding up.

segments.name: Engineering (incl. Praj GenX)
segments.commentary: 22% of revenue and 28% of order intake. Praj GenX won a hyperscale data-center modular supply framework with a minimum of about USD 50 mn over 2.5 years; management said booking is phased, not the full INR 500 crore headline.

segments.name: Praj HiPurity Systems
segments.commentary: 12% of revenue and 10% of order intake. First combined ultrapure water and ZLD contract for an Indian semiconductor company.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; management declined to give margin or segment-level margin targets, citing ongoing investment in Praj GenX, R&D and new ventures.
Praj GenX expected to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27 (management said 'to start with, consider EBITDA breakeven'); PBT breakeven not confirmed.
International order share rose to about 40-43% of Q1 orders; management expects international revenue share to move up from about 25-30% in coming quarters, with export execution from Q3 FY27.
Bio-IBA commercial-scale demo plant construction expected to complete by December 2026.
Management expects new-vertical results (GenX, internationalisation, alternatives to ethanol) to show more clearly in the latter part of FY27, based on current order book.
Material cost upward pressure from geopolitical situation; management said it is using contracts and advance procurement to offset.
capex_capacity: Bio-IBA (bio-isobutanol) commercial-scale demo plant ordered in prior quarter; construction to complete by December 2026. Management cited 2% diesel blending mandate potential of over INR 3,000 crore project opportunity.
Brazil greenfield corn-to-ethanol plant of about 800 KLPD, executed end-to-end by Praj.
Ethanol-to-SAF detailed engineering order from an international customer, following a completed basic engineering order last quarter.

Ballpark capex for a 100 KLPD ethanol/isobutanol plant: INR 100-120 crore, depending on feedstock and product. Praj scope typically 50-60% of project value (process and critical equipment; installation/construction optional).
Mangaluru facility used for Praj GenX precision fabrication and modular manufacturing; first data-center project deliveries expected across Q2-Q4 FY27.
Dr. Pramod Chaudhari Centre of Excellence for Advanced Bioeconomy inaugurated at SPPU on August 10, 2026.
demand_pricing: Domestic first-gen ethanol greenfield inquiries limited to ethanol-deficit states (Tamil Nadu, Assam); management expects this to persist until higher blending mandates are announced.
Funding issues at end customers and ethanol supply-demand imbalance are extending first-gen project execution cycles.
Strong demand for ENA greenfield plants, where management claims a technology edge; brownfield demand driven by efficiency and co-products such as DCO.

CBG: GOBARdhan National Circular Bioenergy Scheme approved with outlay over INR 23,000 crore for FY27 to FY35-36; management expects better CBG margins as market opens, but noted many new CBG entrants.
Margin drag: material cost up about 10% YoY in Q1 on higher African export mix (lower margin); other expenses down about 7% YoY.
Q1 FY27 quarter-on-quarter: material cost down about 3% and other expenses up about 4%, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Collections and execution: why was bioenergy revenue (INR 474 crore) low versus the opening order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to slow conversion of domestic first-gen ethanol projects due to end-customer funding and ethanol supply-demand imbalance, partly offset by acceleration on other projects. Collections are lagging because of slow backlog conversion; management is working on it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin expand, and will RM and site expenses weigh on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said material cost and other expenses offset each other depending on the equipment vs site mix. YoY, material cost rose about 10% on African export mix, while other expenses fell 7%. Management expects steel-driven cost pressure to be managed with advance measures.

qa_highlights.question: Praj GenX breakeven timing and order book share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets EBITDA breakeven by end-FY27 and would not disclose GenX backlog share; engineering is still reported as one basket. Order-book buildup is improving with shorter delivery cycles on data-center orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports decline YoY while domestic revenue rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export revenue timing depends on order entry and execution cycles; a large export order batch was booked in Q1 with execution starting around Q3 after engineering. International share of orders was 40-43% in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory over the next decade and service mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said services margins are higher than project margins and the mix shift (domestic/international, services/projects, new biofuels) is the route to better margins. Current investments in GenX, R&D and new ventures are absorbing margin.

qa_highlights.question: Bio-isobutanol mandate timing and biomaterials (bio-bitumen, PLA)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the timing of any diesel blending mandate is unknown, but Praj is technology-ready. Lactic acid technology for PLA exists; co-product progress is expected by fiscal year-end.

522205|2026-09.headline: Praj Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR 231 million (from INR 192 million) on revenue of INR 8.49 billion; order intake weak at INR 7.15 billion.

H1 FY27 revenue was INR 15.6 billion versus INR 14.8 billion, and H1 PAT was INR 347 million versus INR 246.2 million. Order intake fell to INR 7.15 billion in the quarter, and management said Greenfield ethanol projects in India are stalled by customer funding gaps and feedstock restrictions. Management pointed to CBG, international bioenergy, GenX data-centre and precision-fabrication work as the sources of H2 order growth.

522215|2026-03.headline: HLE Glascoat FY26 consolidated revenue rose 31.7% to INR1,353 crore, but EBITDA grew only 5.4% to INR148.5 crore as Omeras losses weighed.
522215|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR391.7 crore (up 17.4% YoY), with EBITDA of INR43.9 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT of INR20.1 crore (5.1% margin). FY26 EBITDA margin was 11% against a previously guided 16%, with management attributing the gap to the Omeras (Germany) EBITDA loss of INR15.3 crore, a INR2.1 crore labour-code charge and INR4.6 crore of acquisition costs. Management says the ongoing business runs at about 13.5% adjusted EBITDA margin and expects margins to keep rising in FY27. The Board recommended a 55% dividend for FY26, and the order book stood at about INR681.6 crore on March 31, 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Filtration and Drying lag YoY despite pharma order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Ganjwala said execution cycles of 4-7 months mean orders booked now convert to revenue 2-3 quarters later, and revenue is recognised only on dispatch; geopolitical delays also pushed some customer dispatches out by a month or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kinam trajectory for FY27 and FY28 after the large FY26 oil and gas order?

qa_highlights.question: Is FY28 15% EBITDA margin still achievable, and what is the path?

qa_highlights.question: What are the Indian GLE margin and revenue path back to historical peak levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the best year was about INR300 crore revenue at over 18% EBITDA margin, and at around INR300 crore with current cost structure it expects 16-18%; FY27 revenue guided at INR260-280 crore with current visibility concentrated in FY27.

522249|2026-03.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 22% to INR 260.55 crore and PAT 73% to INR 60.71 crore, helped by export mix and FX gains.

qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose significantly as a petroleum by-product and softened somewhat from March highs; availability is no longer an issue. Short-term impact is about a month because pass-through lags, while inventory averages it out long term.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 domestic and export growth, and the volume?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 value growth was 15% overall, with exports about 35.5% and domestic about 4%. Volume sold was 31 million meters, up about 4.5-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins rise to about 30%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers cited were the export mix, currency gains, higher operating efficiency, cost control in other expenses and some March price pass-through. Management guided 25-26% as a base and said 25-30% is possible over the long term.

qa_highlights.answer: Management called 15-20% conservative and said export is running above that. Q4 general export was hit by a Middle East hold and US tariff effects, and the company is targeting new customers and platforms.

qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a provisional impact of the new labour codes (effective 21 November 2025), booked in Q4 as a catch-up, plus some new hires.

Raw material prices softened a little in Q1 but remain above their early-March 2026 levels; prices were very volatile after March.
Shipping costs roughly quadrupled, and the company did not take a price increase on export OEM business, partly offset by about a 10% natural hedge from dollar appreciation.
Management said the company received a 10% price increase in US dollar terms on some business, though it said the US market is softening again.
Competition in PU is intense from China. Footwear demand was muted because sole prices rose two to three times.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% growth came from volume versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew about 2%; the rest came from price, mainly due to an export mix shift to higher-priced items rather than raw material pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin fall sequentially from the previous quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the previous quarter was abnormally high due to a one-time forex gain; the sustainable margin is about 25% plus or minus 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't gross margin improved despite a roughly 40% jump in export OEM?
qa_highlights.answer: The Gulf war raised raw material costs and shipping costs (about 4x). The company had requested price increases from export OEM customers but put them on hold when prices fell, and has not taken an increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR9 crore rise in other expenses QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mixed: higher export shipping/freight, travel, legal and professional, and risk coverage costs. Management said some of this will continue and some will ease; part relates to the subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US OEM growth outlook and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects US business to grow substantially over three years, through wallet share gains with Ford and Chrysler and new Europe RFQs. It declined to give an order book figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% margin sustainable as a base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company should look at annual margin, which can move 1-2% either way quarter to quarter; it aims to maintain the margin level guided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is 65-66% on a 48 million meter total capacity basis (PVC 3.5-3.7 million meters per month); the new line lifts capacity to about 4-4.2 million meters per month and gives 25-30% headroom.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the PU plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The PU plant is underutilised with no change in three months. Sampling with top brands has been done but no business is confirmed, and management cannot make a strong recommendation this financial year.

risks_watch: Freight and raw material costs: shipping cost reportedly up about 4x and raw material prices volatile since March 2026; company has not taken a price increase on export OEM business, so the margin recovery depends on timing of price hikes and freight easing.
US export pricing: a price increase was requested from US customers but not pushed hard; outcome depends on market moves over the next two to three weeks, per management.
Capex and overseas plant: FY27 capex about INR50 crore; a further roughly INR250 crore over two years depends on an overseas plant location not yet finalised (Mexico, US or other NAFTA).
Volume growth: total volume only about 2.77%, domestic about 1%; footwear de-grew on sole price increases; growth guidance of 10-15% is leaning on exports.
PU plant: underutilised with no change for three months, no confirmed business from top brands, and no firm recommendation for this financial year.
Other expenses: about INR9 crore QoQ rise in Q1 FY27 from freight, travel, legal, professional and risk cover costs; management could not split recurring versus one-time amounts.
key_quotes: So, we have not taken a price increase in the export market but you also have to look at one more thing in this 10% more or less natural hedge has happened.
So, we have a headroom to expand to 25%, 30% more capacity.
So anywhere between 10% to 15% growth, we are not looking very strong growth in the domestic market. But yes, we are looking at a very strong growth in the export market.
But this present quarter's margin will be sustainable and expected to continue.

522249|2026-09.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18% to INR282.95 crore and PAT 42% to INR57.99 crore, helped by warehouse stock clearance in the US.
522249|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR282.95 crore (up 18% YoY), with PBT of INR79.31 crore (up 43%) and PAT of INR57.99 crore (up 42%). Standalone revenue was INR252.99 crore (up 6%), with PBT of INR70.46 crore (up 9%) and PAT of INR51.27 crore (up 7%). Management attributed the consolidated outperformance to lower dispatches from India and higher sales from the US warehouse, which cleared its own stock. Export OEM volumes were weak YoY because US auto demand softened, though management said orders are in hand and the trend is improving. Management declined to give formal guidance for the second half or FY28, and the Executive Director was absent from the call due to a family bereavement.

financial_highlights.value: INR90.46 crore (General INR33 crore; OEM INR57.46 crore)
OEM INR62.80 crore; Replacement INR45.02 crore; Footwear INR45.34 crore; Furnishing INR7.19 crore; Others INR2.18 crore; Domestic total INR162.53 crore

financial_highlights.change: Lower QoQ due to Q1 labour-code provision reversal in Q2

segments.name: Export OEM (standalone)
segments.commentary: INR57.46 crore in Q2, below the INR75-80 crore run-rate cited by an analyst; management said it is improving. Volumes were up 13.5% YoY and 5% QoQ, though the export volume YoY was negative per management.

segments.name: Export General
segments.commentary: INR33 crore in Q2. Management expects double-digit improvement, supported by a newly started retail arm in Europe.

segments.name: Domestic auto replacement
segments.commentary: INR45.02 crore in Q2. Volume grew about 11% QoQ and about 5% YoY.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: INR45.34 crore in Q2. Management said volume and value both rose, and guided to 5-10% annual volume growth. Focus is on selected, higher-margin customers.

segments.name: Furnishing
segments.commentary: INR7.19 crore in Q2. Retail is facing price competition; about 750-800 sub-dealers and 8-10 distributors were appointed.

segments.name: PU (polyurethane)
segments.commentary: Revenue booked INR6.28 crore in Q2. Management said the segment is not profitable and operates at about 25% utilisation versus about 40% needed for breakeven.

guidance_outlook: Export OEM expected at INR250-300 crore in FY27 (consolidated basis), versus about INR260-280 crore in FY26 after a confused exchange on the figure.
Export OEM expected to return to INR75-80 crore per quarter from the current level, with improvement described as gradual rather than dated.
Gross margin sustainable at about 55-56%, with variation tied to raw material and crude prices.
No guidance given for H2 FY27 or FY28 top-line or bottom-line; management said the current margin should hold and top-line growth around 20% should continue.
Export OEM expected to grow 10-15% in the following two years, per management.
capex_capacity: New machinery for an additional line: equipment expected in late November to December 2026, installation to begin in the March 2027 quarter, with operations starting in Q1 FY28.
A new plant in India is under consideration, especially in the South region; a Mexico plant is in the pipeline but not concluded.
Capacity utilisation is unchanged QoQ; PU business is at about 25% utilisation against about 40% needed for breakeven.
Bhadla mini-grid solar investment: management cited a payback period of at most 2 years.
demand_pricing: US auto demand weak for two quarters; OEMs revised projections and Q2 US dispatches were deliberately reduced, with warehouse stock cleared instead.
US OEM orders expanded to 5 models from 2 for Ford and Chrysler; BMW and Mercedes-Benz (export OEM) are taking material close to full projections.
Freight and PVC costs spiked from the West Asia conflict and are now easing; management will not pass costs to export customers until increases look stable and permanent.
Footwear and furnishing domestic markets face high price competition; management is deprioritising footwear in favour of higher-margin auto exports.
Pipeline includes VW, plus leather accessories talks in the Kolkata and Kanpur belt; management said new OEM wins take 2-3 years to convert.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of export and domestic auto OEM volume growth, and reasons for weak export volumes.
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic replacement volume grew about 11% QoQ and 5% YoY; OEM volume grew 13.5% YoY and 5% QoQ. Export volume was negative YoY because US customers delayed new car purchases; the warehouse cleared its own stock.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost and other income fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had an extra provision for labour-code changes that was reversed in Q2, so underlying employee cost is about INR12.5 crore per quarter. Other income fell QoQ due to fair-value losses on treasury investments; YoY it rose.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability given volatility (Q1 about 52%, Q2 about 57%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about 55-56% as sustainable, with variation driven by raw material and crude prices.

qa_highlights.question: Transfer pricing between India and the US warehouse subsidiary.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiary keeps the margin needed to cover its local costs and the rest is billed to the subsidiary. Example given: a 10% margin split 8% India and 2% US subsidiary. When consolidated revenue exceeds standalone, the consolidated margin is higher.

qa_highlights.question: Export OEM size and FY26 base: analyst cited INR285-290 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said about INR200 crore for FY26, then about INR260 crore, then confirmed about INR280 crore on a consolidated basis, with FY27 expected at INR250-300 crore. The numbers were inconsistent on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Succession planning after the AGM resolution was not passed.
qa_highlights.answer: The board discussed it; the resolution will be re-proposed with a revised structure after the remuneration and perquisite terms were objected to. A third generation joined about 6 months ago, but Manav Poddar is not directly running the business at present.

risks_watch: Export OEM recovery depends on US OEM schedules; the Q2 export volume decline YoY was attributed to customers delaying new car purchases.
Consolidated growth was flattered by warehouse stock clearance; watch whether standalone growth catches up in Q3 and Q4.
PU segment remains loss-making at about 25% utilisation, with breakeven at about 40%; tax benefits are masking the loss.
Inconsistent export OEM figures given on the call (INR200 crore, INR260 crore, INR280 crore) need reconciliation in the next disclosure.

522275|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 order intake of INR86.1bn (+188% YoY) lifted backlog to INR214.6bn; Q4 EBITDA margin hit a record 27.2%.
522275|2026-03.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported a strong Q4 and full FY26, with revenue up 42% YoY in Q4 to INR16.4bn and 45% for the year to INR62.1bn. Profit before tax and exceptional items for FY26 rose to INR17.1bn from INR8.2bn, and the company ended the year with zero debt and about INR25bn of cash. Order intake was lifted by a large HVDC turnkey order from Adani Energy (VSC technology), and management guided to a mid-20s EBITDA margin for FY27. Management also announced a INR550mn disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu, and a INR10 per share dividend.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Export orders in FY26 were about INR12bn versus INR32bn in FY25, which included one large export order; excluding large orders, base export orders grew 15-20%. Export was about 30% of FY25 revenue and new orders were about 92% domestic.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: Backlog is 98% private customers, central utilities and PSUs; state utility exposure is under 2%.

segments.name: HVDC and projects
segments.commentary: A large HVDC turnkey order (Adani Energy, VSC) was booked in Q4, with execution mainly from FY28-29 onwards. Management does not disclose project versus product split.

guidance_outlook: Management endeavours to deliver mid-20s EBITDA margin going forward, after earlier guiding to low-20s and then mid-20s/high-20s in FY26.
Base order inflow expected to be around INR70bn (INR7,000 crore) and management remains confident of achieving it.
Two pending export RPT orders: a large export order where the decision is expected in H2 FY27, and a U.S. data-centre high-voltage order (about INR14-15bn) expected to be decided in Q1 FY27.
U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group, feeding the Adani HVDC project) expected to be placed in the current quarter; it will not appear in the company's order book.
Capex of more than INR10bn to be phased from early FY27 through FY28, self-funded.
Management declined to give a split of Adani HVDC execution in early years; it said first two years would be lower than 30% and mostly engineering and supply-chain work.
capex_capacity: More than INR10bn of capex initiated across multiple product lines and facilities, to be phased through 2028.

INR550mn approved by the Board for new disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu; disconnectors are being restarted for the Indian market, and some products will be global feeder factory output.
Air core reactor facility and HVDC thyristor valves and controls facility planned in India to raise local content.
Management did not give a revenue ballpark for the expanded capacity, citing that HVDC revenue depends on bought-out equipment and manpower rather than in-house capacity.
demand_pricing: Management says the TBCB pipeline has about 33 packages bid out, 21 of them at 765 kV; the only live HVDC tender is Barmer, whose bid deadline is being extended.
Data centres in India are about 1.5 GW installed, mostly at 220 kV; management expects a meaningful contribution once 400 kV and 765 kV data centres scale.
Transformer contracts carry price escalation clauses; for other products, cost inflation is built into tender pricing.
Management said Q4 domestic order finalisation was slightly dull, which it described as a conscious decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are export orders weak after FY25, and how will the RPT approvals translate into orders in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding one large FY25 order, base export orders grew 15-20%. The pending RPT orders are a large export order (decision in H2 FY27), a U.S. data-centre order of about INR14-15bn (decision expected in Q1 FY27), and a U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and what was the INR50mn Q4 other expense item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintains an endeavour toward mid-20s EBITDA margin. The Q4 other expenses included about INR500mn of notional mark-to-market loss on foreign currency derivatives; management agreed EBITDA would have been better without it.

qa_highlights.question: Is Prolec's U.S. low-voltage distribution strategy relevant to the Indian entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India has no distribution-transformer manufacturing set-up, and entering would need organic or inorganic capacity; it said it does not see that as a current strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani HVDC execution profile and the Barmer/South Kalamb project share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said early-year execution would be lower than 30%, with most revenue from FY29. For Barmer-type projects, the supplier share depends on line length and scope, not a fixed rule of thumb.

qa_highlights.question: Will HVDC refurbishment projects move from LCC to VSC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCC-to-LCC refurbishment only requires valves and controls changes, whereas LCC-to-VSC is a wider scope with higher shutdown requirement and capex; it depends on customer choice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to sustain high margins and growth for longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cycle is broader this time, covering the U.S., Europe, Middle East and Australia, and that export exposure is meaningful; it did not give a timeline for margin moderation.

risks_watch: Customer decision delays on large export RPT orders (H2 FY27 for one, Q1 FY27 for the U.S. order) and their conversion to revenue.
HVDC pipeline timing: Barmer bid deadline keeps being extended, and the next project after Barmer is not clearly scheduled.
Execution of the Adani HVDC turnkey order depends on securing a supply chain, with revenue weighted to FY29 onwards.
Imports of HVDC components (thyristor valves, controls hardware) remain, so local content is still limited until the new facility comes up.
Foreign-exchange derivative mark-to-market charges can affect other expenses and quarterly EBITDA.

key_quotes: So, yes, we remain confident on achieving the base order number of INR7,000 crores.
Our order book remained strong in Q4, and we saw a booking of INR86.1 billion, up by 188% year-on-year compared to INR29.9 billion in quarter ended March '25.
During the fourth quarter, we achieved a record EBITDA margin of 27.2%.
So, this time, the cycle is different. The market is different and the longevity of the cycle looks to be more sustainable.

522275|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion, but order intake fell 30% to INR11.4 billion and gross margin slipped to 41.3%.
522275|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion and PBT rose to INR4.9 billion, with EBITDA margin at 25.1%, within the mid-20s guided band. Order intake fell 30% YoY to INR11.4 billion, mainly on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026, so backlog eased 2.5% QoQ to INR209.3 billion. Gross margin fell to 41.3% from 45.3% in FY26, which management attributed to lower export mix, lower execution savings on elevated commodity prices, and HV business ramp-up. Two large related-party (RPT) orders, INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore, were delayed or on hold, and the company still has no firm plan for surplus cash of about INR16 billion beyond announced uses.

financial_highlights.change: -2.5% QoQ from INR214.6 billion at March 2026
vs 48.4% a year ago and 47% in Q4 FY26; FY26 full year 45.3%

financial_highlights.metric: Total available cash incl. cash pool lending

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export orders about INR5.2 billion of the INR11.4 billion Q1 intake; management says 80-90% of export orders come from GE Vernova group entities. Exports are 10-15% of backlog.

segments.name: Domestic TBCB and grid
segments.commentary: Third-party orders about INR6.5 billion in Q1, per management. Private customers are 77% of backlog, central utilities and PSUs 21%, state utilities 2%.

segments.name: HVDC
segments.commentary: Backlog is back-ended; meaningful growth expected from FY29 onward. Developers' first-phase bids for the next HVDC projects are expected to be decided in August or September 2026.

Management stated it remains confident of the INR7,000-8,000 crore annual base order flow guidance, although Q1 base orders were about INR1,100 crore.
Domestic TBCB market expected flat or up 6-7% in FY27; double-digit growth not expected.

Utilisation: some factories heavily loaded, others have room to grow.
demand_pricing: Q1 order intake down 30% YoY on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026; management says June-July TBCB pipeline is better, but the timing of conversion into orders is uncertain.

Finance cost rose on a INR 18 crore mark-to-market loss on ECB, and deferred tax was higher due to capex-related timing differences.

segments.commentary: Management called FY26 a strong year with healthy utilisation; the last commercialised line runs at optimum level. A fourth line at the unit is expected to be commercialised by year-end FY27, with management expecting its return on assets to beat lines 2 and 3.

segments.name: Folding cartons (consumer products, mainly FMCG and F&B)
segments.commentary: Management said this is more than half of the business. Carton utilisation is lower, with some double-digit scope for growth in existing capacity.

segments.name: Paperboard (Chennai greenfield)
segments.commentary: Utilisation is above 50% and rising on new customer approvals; management expects a good ramp-up ahead.

segments.name: Creative (Noida)
segments.commentary: Management said it just squeaked through to EBITDA break-even in FY25 and improved further in FY26, with a target of cash and net profit in FY27. Electronics demand weakness is a headwind.

segments.name: Recyclable films
segments.commentary: Domestic uptake is weak because EPR rules mandate recycled content, not recyclable packaging. Output is rising through export jobs, and machinery issues are resolved.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin guidance; management expects margins to hold if raw material cost increases stop, and said a prolonged crisis would make further price pass-through difficult.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and which regions could scale beyond the Middle East?

qa_highlights.question: Why is finance cost high despite debt levels, and is the ECB unhedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an INR 18 crore mark-to-market loss on the ECB raised interest cost. It is a notional, non-cash accounting item. Absolute debt grew on a standalone basis and fell marginally on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is deferred tax so high this year and is it linked to capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the actual tax outgo is already reflected, and the higher deferred tax is a timing difference from capex-driven tax vs accounting depreciation. It said the annual tax rate is in line.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give a domestic/export revenue split annually?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will consider providing the split, possibly offline, but did not commit.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any pickup in recyclable film demand, and how is Creative progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic recyclable film demand is weak until the government mandates recyclable packaging. Creative reached EBITDA break-even in FY25, improved in FY26, and management aims for cash and net profit in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and is there a plan to expand into new sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, and calibrated given uncertainty. Management said it adds one or two customers almost every month across sectors and is not sector-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 margins be higher with Chennai and cylinder ramp-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty. It said margins should improve with better utilisation if conditions are better.

qa_highlights.question: Is paper cost still rising, and what is the impact of the minimum import price on board?
qa_highlights.answer: Paper cost pressure continues, with virgin board up sharply and recycled board rising steadily. The MIP on board imports gives domestic mills some room, and management expects some price increase is inevitable.

523301|2026-06.headline: TCPL Packaging Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~79% YoY to INR 40 crore on 16% total income growth, and the company announced a INR 125 crore lithium-ion battery separator film venture.
523301|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 16% YoY to INR 495 crore, EBITDA grew 17% to INR 88 crore, and EBITDA margin improved to 18%. Cash profit rose 56% to INR 76 crore and PAT rose nearly 79% to INR 40 crore, helped partly by a normalised interest cost versus a forex/mark-to-market hit in the prior-year quarter. Growth was domestic-led (good double-digit domestic growth, export growth positive but lower) with volumes up high single digits. Management announced a proposed subsidiary to enter lithium-ion battery separator films (INR 125 crore over 18 months, commercial production targeted Q4 FY28) and a ~30% expansion of flexible packaging capacity (INR 50-60 crore).

segments.commentary: Growth positive YoY but below domestic; prior-year quarter was weak. Management is cautious on near-term global outlook. UK/EU FTAs give slight duty benefit mainly for flexibles.

qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise by ~30% at an investment of INR 50-60 crore; existing capacity is almost fully utilised.

523329|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings rose 120% to INR 744 crores on Solano Gardens launch, while Q4 margins were hit by about INR 14 crores of one-off expenses.
523329|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 bookings of INR 744 crores (up 120% YoY) and collections of INR 352.1 crores (up ~39%), driven by the Solano Gardens launch where 343 of 433 units sold for over INR 384 crores. Q4 FY26 booking value was INR 382.7 crores and collections INR 96.5 crores. Q4 profitability was dented by about INR 14 crores of one-time items (GST input write-off of ~INR 11 crores plus earlier-project costs). The company added ~INR 2,000 crores GDV through three Lucknow land parcels, two via LDA auctions, and guided to ~INR 4,000 crores total GDV across ongoing, unsold and yet-to-launch projects over 5 to 7 years.

Management sees supply, not demand, as the constraint in Lucknow, citing fragmented and disputed land.

qa_highlights.answer: Management credited farmer reach, new R&D products and market credibility. It said monsoon has been good only in pockets, sowing is 15-20% lower, and it cannot project Aug-Sep outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: Will more capacity be diverted to grain ethanol given better sugar prices, and how is ethanol profitability set to move?
qa_highlights.answer: Grain-based ethanol can run up to 260 KLD and will be optimised for margins, which are currently good on maize. Management said it does not plan to add capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR400-odd crore tax reversal and the cash tax impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: It relates to a six-year ITAT-backed position, with MAT credit of INR376 crore. P&L tax stays at 25%, but cash tax outgo is about 19% for at least five years.

qa_highlights.question: Crushing outlook for next season and sugar price expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to call next year's cane harvest given the monsoon. Sugar prices, around INR40-50/kg per the analyst, are expected to stay firm for the next couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for urea margins given global price spikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Urea pricing is governed by FICC rules, so international prices do not hit domestic makers. Government is paying on time; gas price spikes are a pass-through that can strain cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise and what is the year-end net borrowing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt did not rise in Q1; the comparison is year-on-year, covering about INR450 crore of acquisitions and about INR1,000 crore of capex. Year-end net borrowing should be similar, with about INR200 crore reduction possible; debt/EBITDA is kept below 1.5x, with AA+ rating.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the group demerger and expected Bioseed recovery in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is committed to the demerger and aims to file the application with government in FY27, with no firm timeline. Bioseed: large part of Kharif volume is lost and no firm recovery was guided for Q2.

risks_watch: Kharif sowing shortfall of 15-20% all-India, with much higher gaps in Bioseed markets; August-September rainfall under El Nino is the swing factor for SFS, Bioseed and rural demand.
Vinyl: soft Q2 offtake, PVC import surge after the temporary duty waiver, and whether reinstated basic customs duty and US$766/t minimum import price support domestic prices.

Caustic and chlorine: ECU near INR30,000/t and chlorine at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t; caustic utilisation at 82% depends on downstream commissioning, including Bharuch aluminium and calcium chloride in Q2 FY27.
Reported PAT of INR693 crore is inflated by INR474 crore one-time tax and INR79 crore other gains; underlying PAT is INR147 crore, so track the MAT-driven cash tax rate of about 19%.
Fenesta order book up only 4% (about INR1,000 crore), attributed to customers deferring decisions amid the West Asia crisis; margins diluted by new platforms.
Leverage: net debt INR1,649 crore vs INR1,481 crore a year ago, with about INR1,000 crore capex and possible LNG-driven rise in fertilizer subsidy receivables (INR292 crore at 30 June 2026).
key_quotes: So, we normally do not make forward-looking statements, but we do expect the prices; current ECU is in the range of just below INR30,000.
So effectively for, you know, let's say anywhere between 5 to 10 years, at least 5 I can see in the foreseeable future, my effective tax rate will be 19% or tax outgo will be 19%.
And yes, there will be some reduction by about INR200-odd crore probably, but it will all depend how the sugar season pans out, how much will be the inventory.
Our R&D focus is now the key issue which is going to be a major driver going forward, where there is a lot of stress from the management's side.

523367|2026-09.headline: DCM Shriram Q2 FY27 net revenue rose 22% YoY to Rs 3,977 crore, but PBDIT fell to Rs 319 crore from Rs 408 crore on chemicals input costs.
523367|2026-09.overview: Net revenue, net of excise duty, grew 22% YoY to Rs 3,977 crore, driven by Chemicals, Vinyl, Fertilizer and Fenesta. PBDIT declined to Rs 319 crore from Rs 408 crore, as higher chemicals input costs and weaker Agri-input earnings outweighed better realisations, and the prior-year quarter included one-time incentives of Rs 76 crore (Gujarat) and Rs 15.5 crore (sugar power tariff). Vinyl PBDIT rose sharply to Rs 51 crore from Rs 12 crore, while Bioseed posted a Rs 41 crore loss. Management declared a 200% interim dividend (Rs 62.38 crore) and flagged a demerger targeted for Q1 FY28 board consideration.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of the chemicals margin decline on a YoY basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said production costs rose about 6-8% across chemistries while selling prices fell about 4-6%, with coal-linked power the key driver for caustic; hydrogen peroxide was the only product that improved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current PVC price and demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Current PVC prices are Rs 95,000-1 lakh per tonne. Demand expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4 post-monsoon; company running at or above 100% of capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk of Chinese PVC dumping?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Shriram said the MIP of USD 766 plus import duty should keep prices stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said the process is at an advanced stage and the company is targeting board approval soon, with Q1 FY28 as the target timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Vinyl margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said margins improved YoY and QoQ, but future margins depend on energy prices, which are about 60-70% of PVC cost; renewable additions at Kota are expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: What is Sugar crushing and recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Crushing starts first week of November at some mills; cane availability lower due to drought, and UP lodging after September rains may hit volumes. Too early to quantify recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What are the chlorine captive and pipeline levels, and is caustic capacity addition a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive consumption expected at 45% (Bharuch) and 62% (Kota); with pipeline customers about 70%. Aditya Shriram said new capacities should be absorbed over the medium to long term, with new chlor-alkali players integrating chlorine into PVC.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 20,000 crore FY28 consolidated turnover target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said the company avoids forward-looking numbers; it has invested about Rs 4,500 crore over 3-4 years and more investment is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bioseed inventory and provisioning impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Philippines inventory write-off about Rs 12 crore for H1; India provisions about Rs 7-8 crore on government-related receivables, which management expects to recover.

risks_watch: Chemicals margin squeeze: production costs up about 6-8% across chemistries (coal-linked power for caustic) while selling prices fell about 4-6%; management said margins would fall further if prices stay at current levels.
Vinyl margin sustainability: energy is about 60-70% of PVC cost, so margins depend on energy prices; MIP of USD 766/MT plus import duty is the key price support against Chinese dumping.
Sugar crush volumes and recovery: cane availability expected lower from drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka; UP lodging after September rains; visibility only in 2-3 months.

Caustic/chlor-alkali supply: management flagged new caustic capacity and possible near-term supply-demand imbalance; chlorine realisations still negative (about negative Rs 5,000 in Q2, lower again after).

Bioseed and Agri-inputs: weak Kharif acreage, provisions for doubtful debts in India (Rs 7-8 crore) and Philippines write-off (about Rs 12 crore in H1); Shriram Farm Solutions topline timing may reverse in Q3 FY27 subject to crop conditions; urea subsidy requirement could reach Rs 1.2 lakh crore vs Rs 85,000 crore budget.
Demerger timing: board-level scheme targeted soon with implementation around Q1 FY28; management said it wants to avoid a scheme needing later modifications.
key_quotes: So effectively, the margins have got impacted all across except one or two smaller products, but for larger products, it has got impacted.

Going forward, it is difficult to say, although we are hopeful on the prices being firm, as we mentioned in the Chairman's speech as well, that there is minimum import price, which should keep the business healthy.
We generally avoid giving forward-looking statements.
So, we hope to, you know, get it to the Board very soon.

523405|2026-03.headline: JM Financial FY26 PAT rose 46% to INR1,202 crore (ROE 11.7%); Q4 segment profits weak as capital markets deals stalled amid FPI selling.

Management said the IPO pipeline (INR1.4 lakh crore across 55 filings) remains strong and expects the second half of FY27 to be better than the first. Guidance centred on Wealth Management productivity, Private Markets loan book growth of 15-20%, and Affordable Home Loans AUM growth of 25%.

segments.name: Affordable Home Loans
segments.commentary: AUM up 28% YoY to INR3,715 crores; disbursements up 87% YoY; revenue up 22% to INR123 crores; PAT after minorities up 16% to INR17 crores. 151 branches, about 36,000 customers.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Private Markets to meet its guidance; bespoke credit book targeted to grow 15-20% YoY, with about half of that already achieved in Q1.
Capital markets pipeline of about INR150,000 crores excluding Jio and NSE; management hopes to execute a majority of it in the rest of FY27.
Net flows in Wealth expected at minimum about INR6,000 crores for the year vs about INR2,000 crores in Q1.
ROE for FY27 guided in a similar range to last year (about 11.5%) or better; management aims to push Wealth and Asset Management ROE into the mid-to-high teens over time.
Asset Management to get INR150 crores further investment over next 2 years; management targets AMC AUM of INR25,000 crores.
Debt-to-equity expected to rise from 0.8x to about 2x within 3 years as syndication ramps; ARC expected to become debt-free within about 6 months.

Credit syndication income about INR20 crores in Q1.
Industry wealth AUM growth expected at early to mid-teens; management targets above-industry growth.
Mutual fund equity AUM about INR10,500 crores, up from under INR500 crores three years ago; SIP book down about 30% per analyst question, management expects stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cyclicality break in wealth and private credit, and when does organic credit growth start?
qa_highlights.answer: Bespoke book reached about INR3,000 crores, a 5-quarter high, and is about halfway to the 15-20% annual growth guided in Q4. Wealth is a 2-3 year build-out, with FY27 and FY28 expected to be productivity-led.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wealth profitability drop sharply, and will employee costs as a share of revenue fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower transactional revenue and gestation of 100+ RMs hired in 18 months, who take 2.5-3 years to turn profitable. Management said headcount has likely peaked, with hiring now selective.

qa_highlights.question: Asset management SIP book down about 30% and AUM flat; what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-liquid AUM rose 16% QoQ; decline was linked to small/mid-cap concentration. Management engaged more distributors and expects SIP and AUM to recover over the next couple of quarters. Quantitative targets to be shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state ROE is achievable excluding market peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 ROE was about 11.5%, constrained by the 50% NBFC payout cap. Management expects a similar or better range this year, with stronger ROE from Wealth and AMC operating leverage in about 2 years; CACM is about 15% ROE in a weak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Private Markets carries 60-65% of capital and drags ROE; will capital mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity is at a low of 0.8x and will rise toward 2x in about 3 years as syndication grows, lifting ROE into the teens. Dividends constrained to 50% of NBFC profits.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 Private Markets revenue came from the single large ARC transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARC income is lumpy and largely booked on resolution; the June quarter included a big resolution, while book value fell by about INR1,200 crores of recovery and about INR600 crores was redeployed.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for demerger or listing of wealth and asset management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wealth and AM are still small; it will evaluate a listing or demerger at scale, subject to no tax leakage. Affordable housing listing is planned in 2-3 years.

Wealth profitability: PAT fell to INR19 crores as 100+ RMs hired over 18 months mature (2.5-3 years to profitability); watch employee cost ratio and productivity.
Asset Management: SIP book reportedly down about 30%, linked to small/mid-cap concentration; management promised quantitative targets separately, which are not yet disclosed.

ROE drag: Private Markets carries about 60-65% of capital, NBFC dividend payout capped at 50% of profit, and debt-to-equity fell to 0.8x; the plan to lift leverage to about 2x within 3 years depends on syndication ramping.

The month of July, our revenues on the transaction side in Corporate Advisory and Capital Markets for the month of July already exceed what we have done in June, which is a very, very positive sign.

Yes, we can provide them separately.
I would imagine that our current debt equity, which has reached 0.8x, I think we are almost at the lowest.

523405|2026-09.headline: JM Financial Q2 FY27 net revenue hit INR712 crores and PAT INR240 crores, with corporate advisory and capital markets PAT up 4x QoQ to INR127 crores.
523405|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was driven by a sharp rebound in corporate advisory and capital markets after a weak April-May, with segment net revenue up 2.5x QoQ to INR286 crores. Consolidated net revenue was INR712 crores and PAT after minority interest INR240 crores; half-year net revenue rose 7% to about INR1,600 crores and PAT to INR531 crores. Private markets disbursements doubled to INR977 crores, drawing cash down from INR3,077 crores to INR1,691 crores, and management said it will resume borrowing to fund growth. Wealth recurring AUM including loans reached about INR40,000 crores (+17% YoY), while the wealth business only broke even in September.

Deal sizes cut by about INR10,000 crores, costing an estimated 40-50 bps (INR40-50 crores) of fees.

segments.name: Private markets
segments.commentary: Disbursements doubled to INR977 crores in Q2, mainly bespoke; standard loans up 22% YoY to INR4,748 crores. Cash fell from INR3,077 crores to INR1,691 crores; debt-equity 0.8x against a 4x limit. Q2 net revenue INR120 crores, PAT after NCI INR77 crores.

segments.name: Wealth management
segments.commentary: Recurring AUM INR37,000 crores (+16% YoY), recurring AUM including loans about INR40,000 crores (+17%); wealth loan book up 30% YoY to about INR2,600 crores. Sales and RM strength 948 professionals across 71 branches; RM count reduced on productivity. Gross recurring yield about 51 bps and net about 35 bps.

segments.name: Asset management
segments.commentary: First close of maiden Pre-IPO Fund at over INR700 crores; AIF AUM including commitments INR1,063 crores. Average non-liquid AUM about INR11,200 crores (+7% QoQ). MF management fees Q2 INR12 crores (+24%); AMC losses after minority INR10 crores in Q2.

segments.name: Affordable home loans
segments.commentary: AUM about INR3,900 crores (+30% YoY), disbursements +48% YoY, 152 branches and about 37,500 customers. Half-year revenue INR256 crores (+22%) and half-year PAT INR35 crores (+28%).

guidance_outlook: Corporate advisory and capital markets: 15-20% growth over the next 3-5 years; about 15% assumed for the rest of FY27.
Private markets: around 20% loan book growth and around 15% investment book growth; will resume borrowing from next quarter as cash runs to a floor of about INR1,000 crores.

Wealth management: 20-25% AUM growth, subject to market; management expects double-digit recurring AUM growth and full-year profitability in FY28, about three to four quarters later than originally planned.
Asset management: 15-20% growth; SIF platform planned early next year; second performing credit fund first close targeted this financial year.
Group: about 20% blended growth for at least five years; revenue growth of 15-20% should translate into 20-25% profit growth; target mid-teens ROE toward the end of the investment cycle.
Write-backs on impairments: about INR250 crores targeted in FY27, with only INR15 crores achieved in H1; final dividend to be decided on the next two quarters' results.
capex_capacity: Private markets: cash fell to INR1,691 crores; management wants to hold at least INR1,000 crores and will borrow from Q3 FY27 onward.
ARC: after a large account resolved in October (INR330-340 crores liquidity), about INR2,000 crores of SR investments remain, to be realised over 18-24 months at modelled returns of 16-18%.
Wealth: recruitment phase to continue, with a focus on productivity in the next six months; recruiting again from FY28 onward (build-out through 2030).
AMC: building alternatives and SIF platforms; GIFT City and Singapore VCC offerings, with more than USD225 million AUM and USD30-40 million quarterly net additions.
Holding company liquidity: NSE shares listed recently under a six-month lockup expiring March 2027.
demand_pricing: Markets were choppy; primary-market revival from June, with July-September strong and October described as decent; FPI participation returned to primary markets.
Deal sizes were cut, costing an estimated INR40-50 crores of fee revenue in the quarter.
Real estate lending pricing is a constraint: management requires 200-300 bps above corporate, and says there is no stress in its metros.
Broking industry revenue fell in H1 due to regulatory changes; JM says it is holding and gaining cash market share.
Recurring revenue is about 50% of total; brokerage adds 12-15%, so about 62-65% is recurring-type income, with the rest transactional.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the investment banking pipeline depends on market conditions, and is it M&A or market-independent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June revived primary markets; a large part of the pipeline has traded up post listing. Pipeline is robust, and management expects to complete much of it in the next five months if momentum holds.

qa_highlights.question: Will private credit loan growth continue, and what drives the lower yield on cash and investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lending is disciplined and lumpy; it will borrow from next quarter and expects 20% loan growth. Yield dip is attributed to lower real estate lending (priced 200-300 bps above corporate) and the investment book being largely cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why does net revenue in private markets not grow YoY despite higher loan yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to fair value marks, higher cash in the prior year, and recovery-led interest in H1 FY26. Half-year net revenue is up 63% (INR582 crores), and it expects further write-backs of about INR250 crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is wealth growth slower, and what is the RM productivity outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: RM reduction was planned for productivity, with recruitment resuming by FY-end. Broking revenue was flat due to regulation; existing RMs add about INR75 crores net new money each, new cohort about half. Recurring AUM is expected to grow in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why do private markets and corporate advisory not peak together, and why not demerge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARC is largely uncorrelated to capital markets and the bespoke book is linked to it. Demerger has been considered, but synergies with wealth and AMC are high and the company wants to scale first.

qa_highlights.question: Why no large share buyback at a deep discount to NAV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said much of the liquidity sits in NBFCs, and extracting it requires a holding-company tax hit. The NSE stake lockup ends March 2027, and capital allocation will be decided in April-May 2027. Promoters increased their stake by about 1% last quarter.

risks_watch: Capital markets revenue depends on market conditions; deal sizes were cut in the quarter and transactional income is volatile.
ARC and NPA recoveries are lumpy; INR250 crores of write-backs targeted for FY27 with only INR15 crores so far.
Wealth profitability is delayed to FY28; RM productivity and net new money per cohort need to improve.
Private credit yields are under pressure, with real estate priced at a discount to management's required spread; borrowing restart will test margins.
Equity and alternative mark-to-market volatility (e.g., Gokaldas Exports after US tariffs) can swing reported PAT.
Capital allocation: large liquidity in NBFCs and the NSE stake lockup (until March 2027) gate a potential buyback.

523642|2026-03.headline: PI Industries FY26 revenue ₹67,137 mn with ~25% EBITDA margin; Q4 revenue ₹15,652 mn up sequentially, FY27 guided to growth led by H2 exports recovery.
523642|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹15,652 mn, up sequentially as guided last quarter, and FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹67,137 mn with a stated 25% EBITDA margin and ₹34,265 mn cash. AgChem exports declined on lower volumes amid a global downcycle, while domestic demand was hit by channel inventory, price pressure, and lower acreages. Management guided to revenue growth in FY27, with exports recovering in H2, but declined to give a specific growth number or margin guidance beyond maintaining last year's average gross margin. Pharma grew 40% for the year and biologicals are targeted to scale, with the first homegrown NCE (Pioxaniliprole) nearing market.

H1 FY27 was the company's strongest half-year, with revenue of Rs 1,025 crore (+44%), EBITDA of Rs 175 crore (+121%, margin 17.12%) and PAT of Rs 114 crore (+156%). Management attributed the Q2 margin dip to high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses, and more aggressive pricing to win export volumes.

523704|2026-09.headline: Mastek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% QoQ cc to $107.3M, but 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M and EBITDA margin slipped to 14.4%.

Operating EBITDA margin fell about 100 bps QoQ to 14.4%, mainly from increments and ESOPs (190 bps), partly offset by AI-led efficiency and extra working days. The 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M, attributed to a delayed US federal start and slower UK consumption, though it grew 2.3% YoY in USD. Management reiterated that FY27 should beat FY26, with North America turning around from H2 and UK Healthcare recovering after recontracting.

segments.name: APAC & Middle East

Pipeline includes $100M+ deals to be adjudicated over 6-9 months.
