qa_highlights.question: Is the order book weakness execution-led or UK pressure? Is FY27 still expected to beat FY26? What is the ramp on new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: A $25M US federal deal start was delayed until after the mid-term elections, and a UK contract is consuming more slowly than planned, with pickup expected around Q4. Management still expects FY27 to beat FY26, citing H2 strength in UK and US and a Middle East dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are AI deals from new or existing clients, what are the deal sizes, and when will AI revenue be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: AI deals come from both new and existing clients, with at least two net-new wins in the examples shown. Typical AI deal size is $0.5M-$5M, and AI revenue figures will be presented from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin decline, and what is the bridge to the 160 bps recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments and ESOPs cost 190 bps. A UK mix shift from high-margin projects to lower-margin sovereignty and security-cleared work cost about 200 bps. AI-led efficiencies and restructuring recovered about 200 bps. Forex was a 20 bps tailwind. US and Middle East margins are expected to improve from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is North America growth muted, and how do BFSI and healthcare trends differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a North America turnaround from H2. Healthcare & Life Sciences remains its strongest vertical, and BFSI growth is mainly UK-led. North America financial services is still early-stage.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI deals grow after the initial POC, and what margins do they earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI engagements typically expand into more process areas after the first win. Transformation and foundation deals earn 40%+ gross margin, while AI productivity deals carry compressed margins.

523716|2026-03.headline: Ashiana Housing FY26 booking value hit record Rs 2,421 crore (+25% YoY); Q4 bookings Rs 1,290 crore driven by Gurugram Aaroham launch.

Q4 total income rose 46% YoY to Rs 335 crore on handovers in Jaipur, Pune and Chennai, while PAT was flat at Rs 21 crore (6.26% margin). For FY26, total income more than doubled to Rs 1,187 crore, EBITDA rose 281% to Rs 176 crore (14.85% margin) and PAT reached Rs 118 crore versus Rs 18 crore in FY25. Management added about 2.9 lakh sq ft-equivalent of Senior Living land and reiterated a Rs 2,200 crore FY27 pre-sales target.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the counterparty could not obtain social infrastructure approvals after about 18 months, so the transaction could not proceed; the lease was terminated, with scope to restart later.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable presales trajectory over 3-5 years?

qa_highlights.question: Why ROE expectations changed from 20%+ to 15%?

qa_highlights.question: Units sold fell from 407 to 234 YoY. Deliberate or volume slowdown?

qa_highlights.question: Capex for the deals in pipeline and IFC partnership status?

523754|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.8% to INR315.8 crores and PBT to INR16.99 crores, but Q4 PBT fell to INR6.4 crores on a March raw-material spike.
523754|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR315.8 crores (up 14.8% from INR275.1 crores) and PBT of INR16.99 crores versus INR10.7 crores in FY25, despite a INR2.1 crore past-service personnel cost. Q4 revenue grew about 11%, but Q4 PBT fell to INR6.4 crores from INR9.4 crores as PE pipe prices jumped roughly 58-59% in February 2026 and stayed high in March. Receivables built up sharply in a few key subsidy states, and operating free cash flow has been negative over multi-year periods, which an analyst pressed on. Management pointed to non-subsidy share rising to 35% in FY26 (from 3% in FY20 per the call) and to a projects pipeline of about INR54-55 crores for FY27.

523796|2026-03.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q4 FY26 revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 49.5 crore, with EBITDA margin up 183 bps to 31.4%, aided by the Marriott Executive Apartments acquisition.
523796|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 49.5 crore versus INR 36.6 crore a year earlier, and operating EBITDA rose 43.7% YoY to INR 15.6 crore. Growth was driven mainly by consolidation of Marriott Executive Apartments (75 rooms, acquired 1 January 2026), which contributed its first quarter. Management said March was softer on geopolitical tensions and the West Asia conflict, with ADR and occupancy moderating at the existing hotels. PAT fell to about INR 6 crore, which management attributed to higher depreciation and finance costs from renovation and acquisition debt, and to a deferred-tax benefit booked in the prior year.

Phase three is targeted for completion in FY28. Management said the new spa, gym and rooftop restaurant are operating.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 35.3% YoY revenue growth in Q4 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to adding Marriott Executive Apartments (75 rooms, about INR 50 crore annual revenue) from 1 January 2026. Management said the jump will not repeat, but it expects double-digit YoY growth going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 183 bps margin expansion structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin gain came from the high-margin, room-led Executive Apartments and from completing renovation phase one, which upgraded back-end operations and efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the PAT decline came from depreciation versus finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline mainly to a deferred-tax benefit booked last year after the NCLT exit (eight-year loss offset window), plus extra acquisition financing; it did not split depreciation from finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ADR and RevPAR outlook and pricing strategy for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADR fell in March but revenue budgets are protected through occupancy and outdoor catering, and ADR should recover once the wedding and corporate season returns. It also cited weekend long-stay packages and a new spa, rooftop restaurant and secretariat.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost rose from INR 64 lakh to INR 530 lakh in Q4; what is the debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase came from debt taken to buy Marriott Executive Apartments for about INR 215 crore, with debt previously at zero, and that no further rise in interest cost is expected. 523796|2026-06.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 77% to INR44.9 crore and EBITDA rose 144% to INR11.8 crore, with PAT turning positive at INR1.4 crore.
523796|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR44.9 crore against INR25.4 crore a year earlier, and EBITDA margin expanded to 26.3% from 19%. Courtyard reopened with full 168-key inventory after Phase 1 renovation, pushing its occupancy to 83.65% and RevPAR to INR5,006. Combined ADR fell about 12% as lower-paying corporate, army and airline business was added to fill rooms while the Marriott convention centre was offline from April for Phase 2 work. Higher depreciation (INR5 crore) and finance cost (INR5.4 crore, from INR1 crore) absorbed most of the EBITDA, leaving PAT of INR1.4 crore.
